What a ride. Didn't expect to be left questioning loyalty, survival, and how often “I’m trying to help you” means someones about to ruin your life.

After playing every ending, including Phantom Liberty, I changed my mind about some characters quite a few times. It went from understanding someone, to hating it, back to sympathize with them. The world and story excells in showing raw actions and consequences, while not judging directly anyone.

Major spoilers below. Seriously, play the game.

[spoiler]I won't go into the base game, as it allready aged and all loved and hated Johny, but he remained authentic.

Songbird was a tough one. I followed her path first, betrayed Reed, then spent half the journey wondering whether I backed the wrong person. She lied to everyone, to V, used his desperation to save herself. Meanwhile, Reed increasingly seemed like a man who genuinely wanted to get everyone out alive.

Fuck Myers btw. All that talk about duty and saving lives, while people become disposable the second they threaten her political interests. I wished I could have shot her the moment I met her.

I sent So Mi to the Moon first. Killing Reed didnt feel good. He believed in what he was doing, and I really hoped it would work out somehow. So I went back and handed her over. Reed alive, Alex alive, Songbird alive, yet back in FIA hands, but maybe Reed would help her. Seemed like a decent compromise.

Then I took the cure...
After spending the entire game looking for a way for V to survive, I finally got one. Two years in a coma, Johnny gone, Panam gone, almost nobody left. The life V fought so hard to keep had moved on without him. That fucking hurt and all of sudden those 6 uncertain months with people I cared about looked a lot more valuable than they had before.

The Arasaka ending had already left a rotten taste. I felt sorry for Goro, much like Reed: capable, loyal men who believe they’re doing the right thing, serving institutions that are perfectly happy to use them up. Even the rooftop suicide felt like it might spare everyone else until those calls showed what V would leave behind.

So I went back again. Betrayed Songbird in Firestarter. Watched everything fall apart. Alex died, So Mi lost control, and I started thinking she really was the root of the whole disaster.

Cynosure: that Cerberus sequence was fun and scary and I loved it. First time in a while that my V didnt feel like the overpowered killing machine.
Songbirds memories hit: before all this, she was basically a kid who wanted to become a great netrunner. Took a dangerous shot at a bigger life. Sound familiar?
But she didn't have V's luck to remain free for much longer, netwatch would have gotten her soon enough, so Reed thought recruiting her would save her.
Myers turned her into a weapon and kept pushing her into the Blackwall until she was losing herself. By the time she reaches V, Songbird doesn't trusted anyone, and tries anything for survival.
I know it doesn’t erase what she did, but I finally could see her perspective.

I played both outcomes in that bunker. After seeing everything, I came back to the Moon.

Save So Mi. Shoot Reed. Walk away from the FIA cure.

I still feel bad for Reed. Especially after seeing that he could begin questioning his loyalty for the F*ingIA in the other ending. I wished he could have reached that point before.
Also gave that medal to a begger, just like Songbird did.[/spoiler]

All in all it was a emotional roller coaster, absolutely fucking worth it.

So I will end with a quote from Johny:
"Swap meat for chrome, live a BD fantasy, whatever, but at the end of it all, it's the code you live by that defines who you are."

Great game, I've played a few times (PS4 and PC) and would highly recommend, but to me it has a pretty major problem.

My issue with this was that I personally never liked the story or the character you play as (both male and female versions). The main motivation of the protagonist is to run from death so desperately, but they're a mercenary, and it just feels silly that they can kill a thousand people and get shot constantly but then later have panic attacks about their impending death.

This is in stark contrast to the developer's previous masterpiece The Witcher 3, where the protagonist is motivated to save someone he loves and is not afraid to kill everyone on her trail and die in order to do so. That simple concept makes the game more fun, but in Cyberpunk they're simply a gun for hire who wants to be a legend but is their time is running out. That doesn't resonate with me at all.

That is not to say that there are not moments of pretty powerful story-telling. Some quests/subplots are beautifully and poetically crafted and hit pretty hard emotionally, but the main story never did that for me because I just could not care about my character.

For the positives, I think most everything else is very well-done. The gameplay is extremely unique, varied, and fun, and everything/everywhere is visually stunning. Those alone make this an excellent game that I will always recommend—very fun gameplay that doesn't get old, and it's beautiful to look at, but for me the story is just a little lackluster. But it looks like most people don't share my opinion, so hopefully you may find something about the story that resonates with you.

Last thing— Phantom Liberty DLC: fun little expansion but still the same unlikable character and weak story.

After ~150 hours, Cyberpunk 2077 turned into one of my favorite single-player RPG experiences. Night City is the main star: dense, stylish, and full of atmosphere. The story kept pulling me forward, the side quests feel handcrafted (often better than the “main” content in many games), and the characters are genuinely memorable. Combat is flexible and fun - whether you go stealth, hacking/netrunner, blades, or full gun build - and the build variety makes replays tempting.

Performance and overall polish are in a much better place now. It finally feels like the ambitious game it wanted to be from the start: immersive, cinematic, and emotionally engaging, with a soundtrack and visual direction that constantly hit.

Phantom Liberty deserves a special mention. It’s not just “more content”- it feels like a high-quality expansion with a tighter narrative pace, strong spy-thriller vibes, and some of the best missions in the whole game. The new area and storyline add a different tone and intensity, and it’s easily one of the best DLCs I’ve played in years.

If you like story-driven RPGs, strong worldbuilding, and a cyberpunk atmosphere done right -this is absolutely worth your time

This game is... pretty good! Its biggest strength is its setting. It's a joy to pop on the in-game radio and travel around Night City via a car or motorbike. 
Its second biggest strength is its premise. The idea of having the personality of a sh*thead has-been rockerboy stuck in your head after a merc mission goes awry is brilliant. 
This game had a pretty rough launch, but it seems like things have since been ironed out quite nicely, and in my experience the game was rather polished, with only a few janky moments here and there.
The main story was engaging, albeit a bit confusing. I rarely understood what was going on since the dialogue was full of techno-babble and references to various factions and individuals, but I enjoyed it anyway thanks to the vibes.
The core missions were fun. It felt satisfying to blast up enemies with a shotgun, pick them off with a sniper rifle, or slash them to bits with a katana. Sometimes, stealth was necessary as well - and this I found enjoyable too. The gameplay is fairly simple, but the moving story kept things feeling interesting, and the final act was fantastic. The boss fights, though few and far between, were exciting.
Some of the side missions are worthwhile characters-centric detours. Panam, River, Claire, Judy, Brendan and the Peralezes are some of the welcome personalities that populate the world, in addition to main-quest characters like Takemura and Jackie. But, the 'gigs' do expose the core gameplay as quite shallow when it comes down to it, and can be missed without losing much in my opinion. Options such as  quick-hacking and using smart weapons existed, but since the game never posed much of a challenge, these strategies did not ever feel necessary or worth exploring. The skill trees and cyber-ware provided a decent sense of progression, but mostly consisted of simple stat increases rather than providing interesting new abilities that affected gameplay.
Overall, I'd say this isn't a must-play, but might be worth picking up if it's on sale and the trailers intrigues you.

De um lançamento desastroso a um dos melhores jogos que já joguei, enfim, Cyberpunk 2077.
Já adianto que não sou muito fã de primeira pessoa, porém, a imersão com a temática, atmosfera e mecânicas casam muito bem.

Estava procurando um jogo diferente, com uma proposta fora da mesmice e com uma pegada de ação, encontrei ele na promoção e resolvi dar uma chance pra esse jogão.

A história cheia de detalhes e caminhos, personagens cheios de carisma e únicos, carros maneiros e diferentes entre si, armas complexas e simples, combate personalizável ao gosto, ambientação da cidade que, diga-se de passagem, é ÚNICA em todos os jogos atualmente, dando uma imersão absurda ainda mais em primeira pessoa tornando Night City muito viva e diversificada, tornam o jogo uma obra prima simples de entender, gostosa de se jogar e sem ficar maçante mesmo após fazer todo o disponível.

A trilha sonora da rádio é boa e tem uma ligação legal com a história, fora a narração que é impecável ainda mais no PT-BR.

Pra não falar que é mil maravilhas, ainda existem alguns bugs simples como por exemplo um corpo impossível de lootear, iluminação variando, entre outros, porém, em 125 horas de gameplay não fiquei preso em nenhum que tenha bugado a ponto de recomeçar uma missão, precisar morrer para recomeçar ou ficar emperrado em algum canto aleatório.

Üstelik Phantom Liberty ile birlikte bu deneyimin üzerine Dogtown gibi tamamen farklı bir bölge ve casusluk temalı yeni bir hikâye ekleniyor. DLC; yeni görevler, silahlar, ekipmanlar ve yetenek sistemi de getiriyor.

Sonuç olarak ortaya ilk hâlinden çok daha güçlü bir Cyberpunk 2077 çıkıyor.

🌃 Night City

Cyberpunk 2077'nin açık ara en başarılı tarafı dünyası.

Night City'nin her bölgesinin kendine özgü bir havası var.

Şehrin zengin bölgeleriyle fakir mahalleleri arasında ciddi bir fark hissediliyor.

Bir sokakta dev şirketlerin gökdelenlerine bakarken birkaç dakika sonra çetelerin kontrolündeki karanlık bir mahallede bulabiliyorsunuz kendinizi.

Ve şehir sadece görev yaptığınız bir yer değil.

Sokaklarda dolaşmak bile eğlenceli.

Araba sürmek, gece şehri izlemek, rastgele bir bara girmek veya bir yan görev için şehrin başka ucuna gitmek bile atmosfer sayesinde keyifli.

Night City başlı başına oyunun karakterlerinden biri.

🎖️ Hikâye

Ana hikâye kesinlikle kusursuz değil ama özellikle ikinci yarısında oldukça güçlü anlara sahip.

V'nin yaşayacağı süre giderek azalırken oyuncunun önünde sürekli bir soru var:

“Sonunda ne olacak?”

Johnny Silverhand'in hikâyeye dahil olması ise oyunun en önemli noktalarından biri.

Başta sinir bozucu ve kibirli biri gibi görünse de zaman içerisinde Johnny ile V arasındaki ilişki oyunun en güçlü taraflarından birine dönüşüyor.

Keanu Reeves'in Johnny performansı da karakteri akılda kalıcı hâle getiriyor.

Ama hikâyenin bazı bölümlerinde ana görevlerin temposu biraz düşebiliyor.

Bazı yan karakterlerin hikâyeleri ana hikâyeden bile daha güçlü hissettirebiliyor.

Özellikle Panam, Judy, River ve Kerry gibi karakterlerle yapılan görevler oyunun dünyasını çok daha kişisel hâle getiriyor.

👥 Karakterler

Cyberpunk 2077'nin beni en çok etkileyen taraflarından biri karakterleri.

Çünkü çoğu karakter sadece “görev veren NPC” olarak kalmıyor.

Johnny ile ilişkiniz zaman içerisinde değişiyor.

Panam'ın hikâyesi ayrı bir macera gibi.

Judy'nin yaşadıkları Night City'nin başka bir yüzünü gösteriyor.

Takemura ise oyunun en ilginç karakterlerinden biri.

Bu karakterlerin hepsi Night City'nin farklı bir tarafını temsil ediyor.

Ve bazı görevler bittikten sonra gerçekten:

“Keşke bu karakterle daha fazla görev yapabilseydim.”

diyorsunuz.

🔫 Oynanış

2.0 güncellemesiyle birlikte oynanış tarafında ciddi gelişmeler yaşandı.

Artık karakter geliştirme sistemi çok daha anlamlı.

Siber implantlar, yetenekler ve farklı oyun tarzları arasında daha rahat seçim yapabiliyorsunuz.

İsterseniz tamamen silahlarla saldırabilirsiniz.

İsterseniz gizlilik oynayabilirsiniz.

İsterseniz hackleme üzerine kurulmuş bir karakter oluşturabilirsiniz.

İsterseniz yakın dövüşe ağırlık verebilirsiniz.

Bu özgürlük oyunun RPG tarafını güçlendiriyor.

Silah çeşitliliği de oldukça iyi.

Tabancalar, tüfekler, keskin nişancılar, pompalılar ve yakın dövüş silahları arasında seçim yapabiliyorsunuz.

Ve siber implantlarla bunları destekleyebiliyorsunuz.

⚔️ Dövüş sistemi

Dövüş sistemi oyunun ilk dönemine göre çok daha iyi bir hâle gelmiş.

Özellikle farklı karakter yapıları oluşturabilmek çatışmaları daha eğlenceli yapıyor.

Katana kullanıp düşmanların üzerine saldırmak başka bir deneyim.

Hacking üzerine kurulu bir karakterle düşmanları uzaktan etkisiz hâle getirmek bambaşka.

Silahlarla çatışmak ise daha klasik FPS hissi veriyor.

Bu çeşitlilik oyunun tekrar oynanabilirliğini ciddi şekilde artırıyor.

🕵️ Phantom Liberty

Ve geldik DLC'ye.

Phantom Liberty, Cyberpunk 2077'nin üzerine eklenmiş sıradan bir DLC değil.

Bence oyunun en güçlü içeriklerinden biri.

Dogtown'a girdiğiniz anda Night City'den farklı bir atmosferle karşılaşıyorsunuz.

Burası daha kaotik.

Daha tehlikeli.

Daha fakir.

Ve daha kontrolsüz.

DLC'nin casusluk teması da ana oyundan farklı bir hava yaratıyor.

NUSA Başkanı'nı kurtarma göreviyle başlayan olaylar kısa sürede çok daha büyük bir komplonun içine dönüşüyor.

Ve burada Solomon Reed ile Songbird gibi karakterler devreye giriyor.

Özellikle bu karakterler arasındaki ilişkiler ve güven problemi DLC'nin en güçlü taraflarından.

Bir noktadan sonra:

“Kime güvenmeliyim?”

diye düşünmeye başlıyorsunuz.

🏙️ Dogtown

Dogtown bence DLC'nin en büyük başarılarından biri.

Night City'nin geri kalanından farklı bir bölge olması sayesinde oyun yeni hissettirmeyi başarıyor.

Yıkılmış binalar.

Askerî kontrol noktaları.

Kaçakçılar.

Çeteler.

Silah tüccarları.

Ve her yerde hissedilen kaos.

Dogtown'ın atmosferi gerçekten başarılı.

Ana oyundaki şehir yaşamından farklı olarak burada daha kapalı ve tehditkâr bir ortam var.

🎭 Phantom Liberty hikâyesi

Bence DLC'nin hikâyesi ana oyunun bazı bölümlerinden bile daha güçlü.

Casusluk, ihanet, politik oyunlar ve kişisel çıkarlar sürekli iç içe giriyor.

Üstelik seçimlerin bazı sonuçları gerçekten ağır olabiliyor.

Bazı kararları verirken:

“Bunu gerçekten yapmak istiyor muyum?”

diye düşünüyorsunuz.

Ve DLC'nin sonlarına doğru bazı seçimler daha da zorlaşıyor.

Bu yüzden Phantom Liberty sadece ekstra görevlerden oluşan bir paket gibi hissettirmiyor.

Gerçekten Cyberpunk 2077'nin dünyasına ait yeni bir hikâye gibi duruyor.

Steam'deki kullanıcı değerlendirmelerinde de Phantom Liberty'nin Türkçe incelemeleri şu anda %93 olumlu seviyesinde.

🎵 Müzikler ve atmosfer

Cyberpunk 2077'nin müzikleri inanılmaz.

Night City'de araba kullanırken radyodan gelen parçalar bile atmosferi oluşturuyor.

Aksiyon sırasında müziklerin yükselmesi de oyunun temposunu artırıyor.

Phantom Liberty ise bu atmosfere daha karanlık ve gerilimli bir ton ekliyor.

Özellikle Dogtown'da dolaşırken oyunun müzikleri ve çevre tasarımı birleşince gerçekten farklı bir atmosfer ortaya çıkıyor.

🎨 Grafikler

Bugün bile Cyberpunk 2077 görsel olarak etkileyici.

Özellikle PC'de yüksek ayarlarda oynandığında ışıklandırma ve şehir tasarımı hâlâ inanılmaz görünüyor.

Gece yağmur altında Night City'de araba sürmek...

Neon ışıkların ıslak zemine yansıması...

Gökdelenlerin arasında kaybolmak...

Cyberpunk 2077'nin görsel kimliği hâlâ çok güçlü.

Phantom Liberty'nin Dogtown bölgesi de bu konuda oyunun geri kalanından aşağı kalmıyor.

❌ Eksileri

- Açık dünya bazı noktalarda gereğinden fazla tekrar ediyor.

- Bazı yan görevler birbirine benziyor.

- Araç sürüşü mükemmel değil.

- Polis sistemi 2.0 ile gelişmiş olsa da hâlâ kusursuz değil.

- Bazı RPG sistemleri hâlâ tam anlamıyla derin hissettirmiyor.

- Ana hikâyenin bazı bölümlerinde tempo düşebiliyor.

- İlk çıkışındaki teknik problemler oyunun itibarına ciddi zarar verdi.

- Phantom Liberty'nin hikâyesi güçlü olsa da DLC'nin bazı bölümleri oldukça lineer ilerliyor.

🏆 Sonuç

Cyberpunk 2077 benim için çok ilginç bir oyun.

Çünkü bugün oynadığım hâliyle gerçekten çok kaliteli bir RPG.

Ama aynı zamanda:

“Keşke ilk çıktığında böyle olsaydı.”

dedirten bir oyun.

Night City inanılmaz.

Karakterler başarılı.

Johnny Silverhand unutulmaz.

Silah ve yetenek sistemi eğlenceli.

Hikâyenin bazı bölümleri gerçekten çok güçlü.

Ve Phantom Liberty oyunun üzerine ciddi anlamda kalite ekliyor.

Özellikle Dogtown, Songbird ve Solomon Reed sayesinde DLC kendi başına bile çok güçlü bir hikâye sunuyor.

Steam'deki güncel kullanıcı değerlendirmelerinin de hem ana oyun hem Phantom Liberty tarafında “Çok Olumlu” seviyesinde olması, oyunun yıllar içinde ne kadar toparlandığını gösteriyor.

Ama hâlâ kusursuz değil.

[h1]直到大厦崩塌：关于“赢”的谎言[/h1]
[b][u]（含有剧透内容）[/u][/b]⠀
有些游戏是让你赢的，而《赛博朋克2077》是让你认清“赢”有多荒谬的。
接触《赛博朋克》的第一周，解锁“石中剑”黑影车时，特意在公司广场的金鱼全息投影下拍了好几张照片，配上一句[i]“I LOVE NC”[/i]发了动态。那时的夜之城，在我眼前绚烂地绽开：街道上的NPC或吞云吐雾，或因XBD的精神刺激而抽搐；铺天盖地的商业广告包裹着摩天楼的同时，仿佛也将这座城市所谓的阴暗面一并封存。底层市民的廉价消遣，看起来永远无法与V即将完成的宏大事业相提并论。
夜之城最擅长的把戏，就是在一开始骗你。[i]“你是愿意当个无名之辈，一辈子安生，插着尿管死在床上？还是就算活不到三十岁，也要名留青史呢？”[b]Burn out, or fade away? —— Never Fade Away.[/b][/i]
还清晰地记得那个让全世界玩家热血沸腾的预告片。强尼·银手摘下墨镜，那句“把这座城市烧成灰”的豪言壮语，曾让我以为这将是一场轰轰烈烈、改天换地的革命。[b][i]“在这里，你奋斗不是为了赢，甚至不是为了苟活，为的是有朝一日能成为大人物。”[/i][/b]杰克·威尔斯信了，V信了，我也信了。于是我们接活、换义体、变强，全身装满5++的义体。直到孤身一人杀穿荒坂塔，像Neo与Trinity那样，上演“以我残躯化烈火”的奇迹时，这种孤胆英雄主义达到顶峰。在游戏性的层面上，我做到了极致的“成功”：我确实成了大人物，成了来生人人敬仰的传奇。
而《太阳》，把这一切轻轻拆掉了。[b][i]“毁灭你，与你有何相干？”[/i][/b]屏幕上，曾经不可一世的V在缺氧中无措地滑向死亡。随后画面切断，制作人员名单开始无声滚动。我没有哭，也没有愤怒，只是木木地盯着屏幕，看着一个个陌生的名字滑过，心里升起一种巨大空洞的荒诞感。当年那句豪情壮志最终确实兑现了，却以最悲凉的方式收场。它就像一场[b]盖茨比式的幻梦[/b]——[b][i]眼看他起朱楼，眼看他宴宾客，眼看他楼塌了[/i][/b]。我们确实烧掉了荒坂塔，但那种繁华落尽后的空虚却如同余烬般呛人。V没有死在一场势均力敌的史诗决战里，而是死在某种无可挽回的耗尽中。没有阴谋，没有反转，甚至谈不上背叛——因为[b]夜之城从来没承诺过要让你活着[/b]。
在那个瞬间，我突然意识到：V何尝不是另一个层级上的杰克？杰克死在“我马上就要成功了”的幻想里，V死在“我已经成功了”的现实里。夜之城允许你成为传奇，但夜城的阳谋是[i]“夜之城没有活着的传奇”[/i]。它允许你如飞蛾扑火般短暂闪耀，但不允许你拥有未来。
如果说《太阳》是“飞得过高后的坠落”，是对[i]“Burn out”[/i]的[b]惨烈印证[/b]；那么《高塔》，则是对[i]“Fade away”[/i]最残酷的解构——它是一场关于“幸存”的[b]精神凌迟[/b]。
 资料片“往日之影”的译名充满了含蓄美，似乎是百灵鸟对自己过去的追忆；但回归[b][i]Phantom Liberty[/i][/b]，那种冷酷的底色才真正显露无遗。与其说这是关于过去的影子，不如说这是一场[b]“虚妄的自由”[/b]。任务链中的[i]"Somewhat Damaged"[/i]，取自Nine Inch Nails，唱的是[b]伊卡洛斯式的悲剧[/b]；而致敬万青的译名[i]"直到大厦崩塌"[/i]，则赋予了它更东方式的宿命感。那是“如此生活三十年”后的戛然而止，是时代洪流冲刷下，[b]理想景观的彻底淹没[/b]。在《高塔》里，V确实摆脱了Relic，活下来了，但属于V的[b]“大厦”[/b]——那个由义体能力、佣兵身份、伙伴羁绊构筑的自我——彻底崩塌了。这正是任务名称背后最残酷的隐喻。
在《星星》里，虽然V只有半年可活，但有爱人、有家人、有自由，那是在希望中冲向死亡的豪迈，是“向死而生”的浪漫主义。而《高塔》，则是极致的现实主义。V获得了长久的生命，但代价是彻底剥离了让他在这个世界安身立命的根本。你被迫成为了一具被街头混混随意羞辱的肉体凡胎，而那个和暴恐机动队都能打得有来有回的“V震天”，却再也回不去了。
最后，当V独自走在街头，被两个曾经一只手就能捏死的小混混推倒在地，那个瞬间的无力感击碎了所有尊严。也就是在这一刻起，V融入了熙熙攘攘的人群，成为了背景板的一部分。看着那些匆忙路过的NPC，突然意识到，自己也成了德罗斯特口中[b]“插着尿管死在床上”的Mr. Nobody[/b]。没有反转，没有慢动作的特写，没有传奇的背景音乐，有的只是一张模糊的脸，淹没在夜之城的霓虹灯海里。——你活下来了，你治愈了绝症，但你不再是主角了。
[b]这不是一个英雄改变世界的故事，这是一份关于个体如何被世界吞噬的尸检报告。[/b]《赛博朋克2077》没有给我任何廉价的幻想，但它给了我一次极度诚实的体验。正如武侍乐队的贝斯·伊西丝所言：[i]“要想离开夜之城只有一个办法，被装进裹尸袋。”[/i]我很少在游戏里感到这种情绪：不是愤怒，也不是悲伤，而是一种被正面告知“你不可能赢”的冷静。 
太阳不是希望，是[b]最终清算[/b]，它让你燃尽余晖，看着夜之城将你彻底吞噬；高塔不是救赎，是[b]慢性自杀[/b]，它让你泯然众人，看着自己的传奇随风而散。
[b]夜之城没有王，只有结构。[/b]而你，只是一个它讲给下一代听的传奇故事，一个[b]被用完即弃的注脚[/b]。如果你期待的是爽快的英雄故事，漫威式的个人英雄主义，它一定会让你失望；但如果你愿意直视一个成功叙事彻底破产的世界，愿意去体会[i] “云层深处的黑暗啊，淹没心底景观”[/i]的悲凉，这会是一部[b]让你终生难忘的作品[/b]。

Cyberpunk 2077 is one of the best games of all time. It’s genre-defining in both its aesthetic and its story. As an ARPG with a full capital A. it gives you an immense amount of playstyle freedom in its action. You can be a stealthy rogue hacking everything, or a ruthless tank taking hits like it’s breakfast cereal. Or everything in between. That’s where the gameplay really shines, the sheer amount of customization in how your character works. It’s an RPG that becomes an immersive sim in its depth.

This is tied together with one of the best stories in video games, especially for a game with a fully customizable main character. My V felt like a real extension of me, and I got so invested in the story because of the choices V gets put through. That's set alongside not just one of the best main characters in all of video games, but one of the best secondary leads too, Johnny Silverhand, played brilliantly by Keanu Reeves. But don't sleep on the rest of the cast either. close friends who genuinely feel like they care about V. To ambiguous fixers and morally grey but necessary allies.

The world itself is stunning. It’s one of the best-looking games out there. There is not a single shot of the skyline that looks bad. It does cost your PC some performance, it's not a light game to run, but it runs well enough, even with full path tracing. The raw graphics are made even better by the art style, which the game nails to a T. Cyberpunk's aesthetic has never looked this realized. Everything, from cars and clothes, to buildings and weapons, fits perfectly. As a total experience of walking through a cyberpunk world, nothing beats Cyberpunk 2077.

I really recommend this game. I know the launch game had heavy criticism, and a lot has changed since then. Updates have improved it massively, and the Phantom Liberty DLC is a must-play, adding an amazing side story. It's grown into a game that defines its genre, puts CDPR among the best game developers in the world, and creates a world I simply won't forget. A truly amazing game.

This game is... pretty good! Its biggest strength is its setting. It's a joy to pop on the in-game radio and travel around Night City via a car or motorbike. 
Its second biggest strength is its premise. The idea of having the personality of a sh*thead has-been rockerboy stuck in your head after a merc mission goes awry is brilliant. 
This game had a pretty rough launch, but it seems like things have since been ironed out quite nicely, and in my experience the game was rather polished, with only a few janky moments here and there.
The main story was engaging, albeit a bit confusing. I rarely understood what was going on since the dialogue was full of techno-babble and references to various factions and individuals, but I enjoyed it anyway thanks to the vibes.
The core missions were fun. It felt satisfying to blast up enemies with a shotgun, pick them off with a sniper rifle, or slash them to bits with a katana. Sometimes, stealth was necessary as well - and this I found enjoyable too. The gameplay is fairly simple, but the moving story kept things feeling interesting, and the final act was fantastic. The boss fights, though few and far between, were exciting.
Some of the side missions are worthwhile characters-centric detours. Panam, River, Claire, Judy, Brendan and the Peralezes are some of the welcome personalities that populate the world, in addition to main-quest characters like Takemura and Jackie. But, the 'gigs' do expose the core gameplay as quite shallow when it comes down to it, and can be missed without losing much in my opinion. Options such as  quick-hacking and using smart weapons existed, but since the game never posed much of a challenge, these strategies did not ever feel necessary or worth exploring. The skill trees and cyber-ware provided a decent sense of progression, but mostly consisted of simple stat increases rather than providing interesting new abilities that affected gameplay.
Overall, I'd say this isn't a must-play, but might be worth picking up if it's on sale and the trailers intrigues you.

Tive a sorte de jogar Cyberpunk 2077 vários anos depois de seu lançamento, o que me permitiu aproveitar uma versão muito mais completa, polida e próxima daquilo que o jogo sempre se propôs a ser. E posso dizer, sem medo, que foi uma das experiências que mais me surpreenderam nos últimos tempos.

A história principal é simplesmente incrível, com personagens marcantes, diálogos muito bem construídos e momentos que realmente conseguem envolver o jogador. As missões secundárias também merecem destaque, pois não estão ali apenas para aumentar o tempo de jogo. Muitas delas apresentam histórias tão interessantes quanto a campanha principal, aprofundando ainda mais o universo e fazendo com que cada escolha e interação tenha seu próprio peso.

E o que dizer de Night City? A cidade é um espetáculo à parte. Sua ambientação, arquitetura, iluminação e riqueza de detalhes criam um mundo extremamente imersivo. Explorar cada rua, descobrir novos lugares e simplesmente andar pela cidade é uma experiência por si só. É impressionante como o cenário consegue transmitir a sensação de estar em uma metrópole viva, caótica e cheia de personalidade.

Outro ponto que me conquistou foi a liberdade na gameplay. As possibilidades de construir seu personagem, experimentar diferentes armas, habilidades e implantes cibernéticos tornam o combate extremamente divertido. É possível abordar as situações de várias maneiras, e essa variedade faz com que o jogo esteja constantemente oferecendo novas formas de se divertir.

Ainda não tive a oportunidade de jogar a expansão Phantom Liberty, mas pretendo fazer isso em breve. Se o conteúdo adicional mantiver o nível de qualidade que encontrei no jogo base, tenho certeza de que ainda há muita coisa boa pela frente.

No fim das contas, fico feliz por ter dado uma chance a Cyberpunk 2077 nesse momento. Apesar de todo o histórico conturbado de seu lançamento, o que encontrei foi um RPG extremamente envolvente, ambicioso e cheio de personalidade. Uma experiência que, sem dúvidas, vai ficar marcada na minha memória por muito tempo.

Cyberpunk 2077 es un juego de acción y rol en primera persona que, tras una transformación radical con sus últimas actualizaciones, hoy ofrece una experiencia inmersiva y pulida en Night City.
Lo bueno
• Atmósfera visual: Night City impresiona por su diseño urbano, luces de neón y gran nivel de detalle gráfico.
• Historia y personajes: La trama principal y los vínculos con personajes como Johnny Silverhand logran engancharte de principio a fin.
• Jugabilidad renovada: El sistema de combate, las habilidades y los implantes cibernéticos permiten crear estilos de juego muy variados.
Lo malo
• Conducción: El manejo de los vehículos se siente algo ligero y poco preciso.
• Expectativas de mundo abierto: Aunque la ciudad luce viva, algunos sistemas de interacción y la profundidad del entorno abierto se quedaron cortos frente a lo prometido inicialmente.

Cyberpunk 2077 is one of my favorite games of all time, and in its current state I absolutely recommend it. I also want to be fair about it, because pretending the launch disaster never happened would be dishonest. It released in a horrible state, especially on older consoles, and it deserved criticism for that. But judging the game as it exists now, this thing is excellent.

What kept winning me over was the sheer feel of it. Night City still looks absurdly good. The lighting is ridiculous, the atmosphere carries almost every scene, and even years later this game still has moments where you just stop and stare at the environment. It is not just technically pretty, it has style, mood, and identity everywhere. Few games sell a place this well.

The other big strength is that the game is just fun to play when your build comes online. Cyberpunk absolutely nails the power fantasy. Once you get some real chrome installed and your build starts working the way you want, combat becomes a blast. Slow-mo, shotguns, LMGs, cyberware, explosions, chaos, all of it feels great. I spent a lot of this run doing side content simply because moving through the world and deleting enemies was enjoyable on its own.

Story-wise, I think it is very strong, especially in the character writing. The game has a lot more texture than people give it credit for. Even side gigs often have enough personality, weirdness, tragedy, or moral grime to make them memorable. Phantom Liberty in particular is outstanding. I think it is the best content in the game. It feels tighter, meaner, and more focused, with some great spy-thriller energy layered on top of the base game’s drama.

I do still have a few complaints. The game can still be janky. I ran into weird NPC behavior, some visual glitches, odd physics, and the occasional quest jolt. Nothing here ruined the experience for me, but the game still has rough edges. The driving is also inconsistent. Some cars feel amazing, some feel like boats with wheels. And the main story’s urgency can clash with the open-world design, because the narrative tells you your life is collapsing right now while the game also wants you to go do fifty side jobs and boxing matches.

Still, the good outweighs the bad by a mile. Cyberpunk 2077 now feels like the game people wanted it to be in the first place: gorgeous, stylish, mechanically fun, full of personality, and backed by genuinely strong story content. It is not flawless, but it is absolutely worth playing, and Phantom Liberty only makes that more true.

早上好，夜之城！
打算买这款游戏是在看完边缘行者之后，伴随着《多想留在你房间》的音乐，看着剧中仿佛无敌的亚当重锤，感受到了一种深深的悲剧与无力感，于是决定买个游戏进去暴打重锤一顿，游戏的主线其实几句话就能概括，但置身于赛博朋克的底色下，以v的视角亲身见证了形形色色的人和事，他们都是那么的鲜活，跳动在夜之城这颗心脏上。赛博朋克的底色是悲剧——起码对于处于中底层的人们来说。炸了荒坂塔，却在原本的废墟中矗立了一座更高的荒坂；v就算是主人公，最好的结局也是再活一年不到。但正如那句话所说：“世界上只有一种真正的英雄主义，那就是在认清生活的真相后依然热爱生活。”真正的人生从来不是一帆风顺，也不是热血少年漫中主角喊着朋友的羁绊就能一拳干翻幕后大boss那样容易，但哪怕前面有种种困局在等着你，也要“以我残躯化烈火”去燃尽它们。
“永远不要放弃战斗，V。”
尽管之前因为周围有人硬洗2077的bug（觉得游戏没有bug全是玩家自己的问题）使得我对于这款游戏有极大的偏见，但是在放下偏见实际游玩之后，我不得不感叹游戏的内核给我带来的震撼，过于真实以至于问我未来世界是什么样子我第一时间想到的只会是2077

我记得我第一次打开2077的时候仍然在备战考研，2077成为了继辐射四之后，我当时不得不卸载以阻止自己玩下去的第二款游戏，那种神奇的让人实在是忍不住继续下去的感觉，让我恍惚意识到已经过去了五年时间。
如今我多次带着执念，坚持让自己在这个周末的尾巴坚持写下这些，因为我突然意识到，我并不能保证自己还能不能再像今天，像之前一样那么为这样一款游戏而感到深深的着迷。
我真的觉得cdpr做到了，在今天看来，他们真的做到打造了一个迷幻，破碎，遥远的赛博朋克世界，并且真的让人深深的着迷。
在这里，人们带着麻木且悲哀，又带着那么点轻蔑地倔强生存着，像一群蚂蚁一样没完没了为了蝇头小利甚至莫名其妙的事情争斗，把人命吹的比纸还薄，把钱看的比什么都重，在野蛮秩序生长的科技加持下，道德，伦理，人性被无限放大，缩小，扭曲。可就是在这样的迷幻又抽象的漩涡里，cdpr的叙述，v的视角，像是一只碳素笔。
刚开始看似简单勾勒，但越走近就越发现，那些霓虹灯光泛滥的楼宇，和看见就让人心驰神往的摩天大厦之间，夹杂着那么多欲望，那么多不甘。
你忍不住向前，就会发现那些灯光和绚丽，实际上都是一个个被资本和科技挤压成齑粉的灵魂，每个人都在用竭尽所能的力气活下去，做他们力所能及的反抗，看到他们的失落和不甘。
而朱迪，我很久没有看到如此丰满让人着迷的形象了，仿佛真的可以穿透电子屏幕感受到她的气息，感受到被刻画的栩栩如生的，带着点偏执，在重压下挣扎又渴望幸福的孤独灵魂。

但是也有很多可惜的地方，受制于篇幅，受制于技术能力，受制于工时。

我还是情愿相信，如果真的，未来可以把当时的设想都还原出来，那该是一款多好玩的游戏啊。

当然了，现在也是一款值得认真玩的好游戏。
虽然刚发售的时候，写差评的里面有80%的人都是没买过游戏的臭傻逼。当然了，尤其是在B站的弱智游戏评测平台上打差评的臭傻逼。
总而言之，时隔这么多年回来重头玩到尾，它在我心目中仍然是属于特别好评的神作，当然了，事实也本该如此。

当我第一次听说这款游戏时我早已被它的世界观深深震撼，那时我还没有属于自己的电脑只能在手机上来填补我对它的期待，在发售之前我和很多人一样对这座充满传奇的城市备受期待，就像流浪者V一样在夜之城名扬天下，但是没有什么是一帆风顺的，《赛博朋克2077》的首发让很多人对CDPR感到失望，当然这并未浇灭我对《赛博朋克2077》的热情。在没有电脑的日子我一直在详细地了解赛博朋克，主要以影视的方式为主，例如《银翼杀手》系列、《攻壳机动队》、《阿基拉》等等。我被他们的风格和世界观深深吸引就像第一次认识2077一样，这激发了我想进入夜之城的热情。我第一次开始启动《赛博朋克2077》是在一家网吧（也可以说我进网吧玩的第一款游戏）屏幕是显示黄色的赛博朋克2077的字样时我无疑是兴奋，在出现第一句“早上好，夜之城……”出现时，它极大的刺激着我前往夜之城。在选择主角V出身时我选的流浪者（因为之前看人家主播玩的时候人家选的是流浪者）之后我操作着V开着刚修好的小车去找杰克碰面，并一起跨越边防后歪打正着成为最好的搭档然后又立下要名扬天下成为夜之城的传奇，不过想成为传奇的代价是死，说实在的我第一次看到杰克的死并无多少感想，一直认为是cdpr为赶进度的强行剧本杀，直到二周目重新参加杰克的葬礼我才开始对他有所情感，也让我意识到在夜之城比成为传奇更重要是家人和朋友，现实也是如此我们可能会因为学业和事业而忽略家人和朋友，我认为和家人坐下聊聊天或者叫上朋友出去耍起比什么都重要。夜之城是一座值得探索的城市，在玩到强尼第一次出现时，我想每个人之所以会被他吸引不仅仅是他是有基努里维斯出演还有他的敢于反抗的精神（我认为强尼的中配占据大头）很难想象V和强尼第一次见面唯一的共同想法是让对方滚出去，到最后双方都想让对方好好活下去，这其中V和强尼经历太多V教会这个死了五十的年且狂热的老疯子学慢慢地会平庸并让自己意识到过去的行为有多傻吊并且慢慢学会理解他人，而强尼教会这个二十多岁想名扬天下却中途挂掉的愣头青认识形形色色的人也教会他敢于战斗去反抗，也一步步地引导V成为夜之城的传奇（说真的这对组合挺招人稀罕的一个只想活命的愣头青和一个只是复仇的狂热的老毕登…）好吧o(￣ヘ￣o#)我还是聊聊强尼·银手吧，首先我之前看的关于赛博朋克风格的影视它们让我看到赛博朋克的世界是什么样的:霓虹灯，全息投影和义体改装，从视觉让我体会到什么是赛博朋克风，而强尼·银手这个核爆荒坂塔的男人，他的前后经历让我理解什么是赛博朋克。当我操纵V完成巫毒帮或者赫尔曼的委托时结果并不是我们想要的当V心灰意冷时，强尼站了出来他给V解释他为什么执意跟荒坂过不去直到他说出整个游戏的核心内涵之一“我目睹过公司夺走农民的水源…最后是土地，还目睹过夜之城变成一台机器，用人们崩溃的精神，破碎的梦想以及民脂民膏来做燃料，长久以来公司控制着民生，拿走了一切…现在就连灵魂也不放过。V，我宣战，不是因为资本主义是我的眼中钉，也不是为了怀念过去的美国才怎么做的，这他妈是一场人民反抗脱缰社会体制的战争，也他妈是一场对抗乱世的战争，你明白吗，必须不计代价地阻止他们，战胜他们，撕碎他们，需要杀人我就去杀，需要你的身体，我就拿走你的身体…”这是强尼让人们喜欢他的原因之一他给我展现了真正的夜之城是什么样，真正的赛博朋克是什么样。他是赛博朋克的内涵也是2077的魅力所在。最后再聊聊2077的dlc《往日之影》他不仅丰富的《赛博朋克2077》的世界观，也给我带来了前所未有的惊喜。这是一部值得深思的谍战题材的作品，虽然他的整体基调充满悲观色彩和人性的不堪从百灵鸟的欺骗，李德的愚忠和迈尔斯的野心，但每一个角色都被CDPR刻画的十分立体。说真的我对百灵鸟并没有多少好感度，她从头到尾一直欺骗V…额不对应该是所有人，整个往日之影给我最大的感受只有两个1.人人都需要V，但人人都不在乎V、 2.天上没有免费的馅饼o(￣ヘ￣o#)（最后我还是把她送上火箭）不过《往日之影》确实让《赛博朋克2077》焕发了第二春，也是玩家在首发灾难后收到的一份满意的答复。通关游戏后我觉得有两个结局值得聊一下，分别是“以我残躯化烈火”和“自杀结局”，以我残躯化烈火是V和强尼一起单枪匹马杀进荒坂塔不让任何伙伴替V送命，强尼让V领悟的成为传奇的秘诀，很难想象一个还有半年寿命的街头佣兵和一个死了五十多年的狂热恐怖分子一起杀进荒坂塔，V死了亚当·重锤替强尼报仇，而强尼一路陪伴着V直到进入神舆…我认为以我残躯化烈火是V和强尼双向成长的最好答复V像强尼，强尼像V从“城市之王”中的V不惧任何风险完成委托到“节制”中的强尼变得“碌碌无为”感叹夜之城的美好（放以前强尼会说“夜之城就是他妈的一座化粪池而且每时每刻还有不少2B往里面跳”o(￣ヘ￣o#)）我想这个结局是非常值得体验的结局。如果说“以我残躯化烈火”是《赛博朋克2077》的巅峰之作而“自杀结局”是考验CDPR心细和功底的最好展现，想想看目前很少厂商和作者能像《2077》那样敢把主角自杀直白的展现出来，主角自杀这个话题向来是极其敏感，如果弱化自杀就没多大含义，如果把自杀写的很醒人耳目容易会背上宣传自杀的意图。我第一次我这个结局为什么会有这个结局总感觉这个结局是来凑数的，并未有什么感受只觉得疑惑，但在结尾V的朋友们打来的电话有人自责，有人悲伤，有人愤怒，有人不解。整个结尾让人看着不想再体验第二遍，直到有人解释这个结局只是给一少部分人看的，因为从V选择自杀那一刻，强尼先会劝一下V到朋友们对V的各种感受这其中包含着强烈的反自杀倾向，自杀后你的家人和朋友只会感到悲伤，只会显得自己很不负责不把自己亲近之人当回事，我认为CDPR在这方面下了很足的功夫也侧面展现他们的功底和用心。这两个结局是我认为CDPR的用心之作。最后还是催促一下CDPR抓紧开发《赛博朋克2》期待下一步巨作。(•‿•)

One of the best games ever. Seriously.

When it first launched, I played it on a friend’s PC. There were a lot of bugs back then — but honestly, they never stopped me from enjoying the game. The core experience was already strong. And now? It’s been massively improved, polished, expanded — it feels like a completely different level of quality.

The world-building is incredible. Night City feels alive, layered, immersive. The characters are all compelling in their own way. The overall design — environments, fashion, UI, everything — is just cool. And the soundtrack? Absolutely great. Morro Rock Radio always fits the vibe perfectly.

As someone who mostly plays story-driven games, I did have some mixed feelings about the romance options for female V. It sometimes felt like the partners get very attached very quickly. I personally prefer something more balanced — that’s why I actually like the dynamic with Panam (even though you can’t romance her as female V in the base game). She feels like a fully independent character with her own life and priorities.

I just wish there was a bit more variety in relationship dynamics — maybe more shared activities, more different emotional tones. Everyone has their own preferences, of course, but for me the romance paths for female V felt a bit too centered on intense attachment.

That said — everything else? I loved it. Leveling up is fun. Experimenting with builds is fun. Exploring is fun. The story hits hard.

I 2077% recommend playing this game. And trust me — you won’t finish it just once.

Great game, I've played a few times (PS4 and PC) and would highly recommend, but to me it has a pretty major problem.

My issue with this was that I personally never liked the story or the character you play as (both male and female versions). The main motivation of the protagonist is to run from death so desperately, but they're a mercenary, and it just feels silly that they can kill a thousand people and get shot constantly but then later have panic attacks about their impending death.

This is in stark contrast to the developer's previous masterpiece The Witcher 3, where the protagonist is motivated to save someone he loves and is not afraid to kill everyone on her trail and die in order to do so. That simple concept makes the game more fun, but in Cyberpunk they're simply a gun for hire who wants to be a legend but is their time is running out. That doesn't resonate with me at all.

That is not to say that there are not moments of pretty powerful story-telling. Some quests/subplots are beautifully and poetically crafted and hit pretty hard emotionally, but the main story never did that for me because I just could not care about my character.

For the positives, I think most everything else is very well-done. The gameplay is extremely unique, varied, and fun, and everything/everywhere is visually stunning. Those alone make this an excellent game that I will always recommend—very fun gameplay that doesn't get old, and it's beautiful to look at, but for me the story is just a little lackluster. But it looks like most people don't share my opinion, so hopefully you may find something about the story that resonates with you.

Last thing— Phantom Liberty DLC: fun little expansion but still the same unlikable character and weak story.

[h1]Un avis plus structuré et plus pertinent 10/10[/h1]

[i]Cyberpunk 2077 est un chef-d'œuvre marquant, une expérience intense et inoubliable. Avoir exploré la ville dès sa sortie le 10 décembre 2020, traversé son lancement difficile, pour finalement y passer plus de 1350 heures sur GOG et le finir deux fois à 100 %, cela donne un recul unique. Ce jeu est devenu l'un de mes favoris, et voici pourquoi il est indispensable d'y jouer, expliqué de manière logique et fidèle au jeu.[/i]

[h2]🏙️ Night City : Un choc visuel et une ambiance folle[/h2]

La plus grande réussite du jeu, c'est sa ville. Ce n'est pas juste un décor, elle est vivante, sombre et fascinante.

[b]• Des quartiers avec une vraie identité :[/b] On passe sans transition des grandes avenues riches tenues par les corporations (les mégas-entreprises qui dirigent le monde) aux ruelles sales et dangereuses des bas-fonds. Chaque district a son propre style et sa propre criminalité.

[b]• La magie des néons la nuit :[/b] C'est quand le soleil se couche que le jeu devient incroyable. Les lumières artificielles sous la pluie et la sensation de gigantisme vertical (les gratte-ciels immenses qui vous écrasent) créent une atmosphère dystopique (un futur sombre et pessimiste) totale. On s'y perd avec un plaisir fou.

[h2]🎭 Une histoire comme au cinéma et des choix importants[/h2]

Le point fort du jeu, c'est son écriture et la façon dont la mise en scène nous implique directement au cœur du récit.

[b]• Une réalisation au plus près de l'action :[/b] Tout est fait pour qu'on ne décroche jamais de l'histoire. Les cinématiques et les discussions s'intègrent directement au jeu sans aucune coupure. Cela donne l'impression de vivre un film interactif très réaliste, où la tension des scènes violentes et l'intimité des moments calmes nous touchent de plein fouet.

[b]• Des choix qui changent votre parcours :[/b] Vos origines (Nomade, Gamin des rues ou Corpo) et vos décisions ouvrent différents embranchements. Vos choix modifient le déroulement des contrats, vos relations avec les personnages et même la conclusion de l'histoire principale. C'est ce qui donne envie de recommencer le jeu plusieurs fois.

[b]• La cohabitation avec le fantôme de Johnny Silverhand :[/b] Être bloqué dans sa propre tête avec le construct psychique (la conscience sauvegardée) de ce rockeur rebelle change complètement l'aventure. On a la sensation permanente de parler à un véritable fantôme qui hante vos pensées. Johnny est toujours là, invisible pour les autres, à vous observer. Il passe son temps à juger absolument tout ce que vous faites : vos alliances, vos contrats, vos réactions avec les autres personnages et vos choix moraux. Ce parasite cynique n'hésite jamais à donner son avis bien tranché, souvent provocateur, ce qui rend l'expérience incroyablement immersive et unique.

[h2]⚔️ Gameplay : De l'action rapide et une liberté totale[/h2]

Manette ou clavier en main, les combats sont nerveux, fluides et très amusants.

[b]• Des combats dynamiques :[/b] L'action est rapide, agressive et rythmée. Qu'on utilise des armes à feu ou qu'on se batte au corps à corps (comme au katana), les sensations sont excellentes et on ressent bien l'impact des coups.

[b]• Un arsenal géant :[/b] Il y a une variété d'armes incroyable. Entre les armes cinétiques classiques, les armes intelligentes dont les balles suivent les cibles et les armes iconiques uniques avec des pouvoirs spéciaux, chacun trouve sa façon de combattre.

[b]• Le Cyberware (les implants) :[/b] Vous pouvez modifier le corps de votre personnage chez un Charcudoc (chirurgien de rue) pour changer complètement votre style de jeu. Devenir un prédateur ultra-rapide capable de ralentir le temps avec le Sandevistan, ou devenir un Netrunner invisible capable de pirater le système nerveux des ennemis à distance, offre une liberté totale.

[h2]📝 Le Verdict[/h2]

Cyberpunk 2077 est l'histoire d'une rédemption (un retour au sommet après un échec) incroyable. C'est un voyage émotionnel fort, porté par un univers cohérent et un gameplay ultra-plaisant. Ne pas y jouer, c'est rater un monument du jeu vidéo moderne.

La ville vous attend, avec le choix ultime qui fera votre légende : [i]Une vie paisible ou une mort spectaculaire ?[/i]

Cyberpunk 2077 has come a long way and now feels like a genuinely great experience. After a rough launch, the game is much more stable and enjoyable, and it finally shows what it was meant to be.

Night City is easily one of the game’s biggest strengths. The city feels alive, dense, and full of style, and the cyberpunk atmosphere really hits. The main story is engaging, sometimes dark, sometimes emotional, and a lot of side quests are surprisingly well written, to the point where they really stick with you after you finish them.

The gameplay gives you a lot of freedom. You can focus on hacking, stealth, guns, or melee combat, and play the way you want. Character progression feels rewarding, and you really feel your character getting stronger and more efficient over time.

I played the game with mods, and honestly, it makes a huge difference. The graphics look even better, the city feels more immersive, and outfit mods add a lot of style and variety. Being able to fully customize your character and their look makes the whole experience even cooler. With mods, the game can look absolutely amazing.

From a technical point of view, the game is now in a very good state. The visuals are great, especially on a decent PC, the lighting looks fantastic, and the soundtrack fits Night City perfectly. The voice acting and sound design also do a great job at pulling you into the world.

Overall, Cyberpunk 2077 is absolutely worth playing now. I’d definitely recommend giving it a shot and diving into Night City.

Cyberpunk 2077 ist doch noch das erhoffte Meisterwerk geworden, dass sich CD Red schon beim Launch erhofft hatte. Immerhin hat sich die Hardware in den letzten Jahren so weit entwickelt, dass es mittlerweile auch gut auf Einsteiger- und Mittelklasse-PCs läuft. Ganz ungetrübt endet mein Spielerlebnis jedoch nicht. Sowohl inhaltliche Schwächen als auch technische Probleme gibt es auch heute noch. Trotzdem ist Cyberpunk eines der besten Spiele aller Zeiten, über das man auch noch in 20 Jahren reden wird.

Die Technik
Ich habe auf mittelhohen Einstellungen mit leichtem Raytracing und DLSS 3 gespielt, was meist gut lief. Trotzdem gab es so viele Abstürze wie bei keinem anderen Game, hin und wieder wurde meine Hardware durch Wechsel von Zwischensequenzen und beim öffnen der 3D-Karte überfordert. Optisch haut einen das Spiel auch noch über 100 Stunden noch um und muss sich nicht vor Genre Größen wie GTA V verstecken.

Die Story
Überraschend komplex, oft tiefsinnig und viele Entscheidungs- und Verlaufsmöglichkeiten. Cyberpunk fühlt sich hochwertig geschrieben und die Charaktere lebendig an. Keine Klischees, keine 0815-Story-Bits, hier wird man als Liebhaber guter Geschichten ernst genommen.
Das Pacing fand ich hingegen befremdlich. Selbst wenn man wie ich gern vom Weg abgeht und lieber die nächste spannende Nebenquest statt die Mainstory verfolgt, landet man hier gerne mal nach 30 Stunden bei der finalen Mission. (Ohne Addon) Das empfand ich als ungewohnt, zumal viele Nebenerzählungen in mehreren Quests ablaufen und teilweise nochmal weitere Story-Überraschungen und Quests hervorbringen. Man verbringt also eine ordentliche Portion Spielzeit mit dem abgrasen von Map-Icons, wenn man denn alle Welt-Aufträge erledigen möchte.

Die Quests
Quests sind allgemein stets interessant und abwechslungsreich, das sind wir ja schon aus Witcher 3 gewohnt gewesen. Das gilt teilweise sogar für die anfangs generisch wirkendenden, unzähligen Sonderaufträge (grüne Rechtecke mit Ausrufezeichen), die man überall auf der Map erledigen kann und allein wahrscheinlich schon 30-40 Stunden dauern können. Wirklich generisch und am Ende auch etwas nervig sind jedoch die NCPD-Locations, bei denen man Verbrecher unschädlich machen und Beweise sichern soll. Nicht nur sind diese immer nach dem gleichen Muster aufgebaut (nur mit unterschiedlichen Locations), es spielt auch keine Rolle ob man sich als unsichtbarer Cyber-Ninja durch die Goons schleicht, oder einfach alles nieder metzelt. Hier fehlte mir Tiefe und Anspruch.
Das gleichen jedoch die cinematischen Story-Quests mit interessanten Geschichten und teilweise knackigen Boss-Kämpfen wieder aus. An dieser Stelle sei zu loben: Trotz hohem Schwierigkeitsgrad kam es bis auf eins, zwei Ausnahmen nie zu Frustmomenten. Das Gameplay gibt einem genügend Werkzeuge für jede Vorliebe der Kampfkunst an die Hand. Auch crazy Herausforderungen wie das verzichten auf jegliche Tötung von Gegnern sind möglich. Cool!

Das Gameplay
Auch sonst fühlt sich Cyberpunk - nach einer kurzen Eingewöhnungsphase - vertraut gut an. Fahrzeuge steuern sich angenehm (Motorräder habe ich gemieden), Kämpfe sind je nach eigenem Anspruch spaßig und abwechslungsreich. Auch die Stealth-Mechaniken, die ich immer wieder gern eingesetzt habe, funktionieren gut, sind aber auch realistisch und anspruchsvoll. Lediglich die KI offenbart in solchen Situationen ihre Schwächen, Gegner verhalten sich immer noch so hohl wie schon vor 15 Jahren in solchen Spielen.
Ein Tipp für das erkunden der Stadt: Ganz oft lohnt es sich, das Auto stehen zu lassen und zu Fuß durch die engen Gassen und vielen Treppen und Ebenen der Stadt zu laufen, es gibt abseits befahrbarer Wege mehr zu entdecken als man zunächst annehmen könnte. Auch das klettern offenbart immer wieder kleine Geheimnisse und große Ausblicke.
Was ich nicht ganz verstanden habe sind die erwerbbaren Unterschlüpfe, bei denen sich eigentlich nie ein Besuch lohnt, auch nicht für den Besuch der Freundin/des Freundes: Diese nachträglich angebaute Mechanik fühlt sich weder ausgereift noch spaßig an. Man kann einfach keine gemeinsamen Aktivitäten machen ... außer schlafen. Da vermisse ich doch glatt die Bowling-Nachfrage von Roman. Auch sonst gibt es keine Nebenaktivitäten außer die sehr liebevoll gestalteten 3 (?) Arcade Games, wo auch Roach (unser Lieblingspferd) ein Comeback feiert.

Noch ein paar Worte zum skillen und dem Charakteraufbau: Ich war oft überfordert und frage mich immer noch, ob es all diese Systeme und Mechaniken, z.B. auch das Crafting wirklich gebraucht hätte. Hier verliert man schnell die Übersicht.

Das Addon
Phantom Liberty ist mehr vom gleichen, gepackt in eine weltumspannende Agentenstory abermals mit schweren Entscheidungen. Wer Cyberpunk 2077 durchspielen möchte, sollte sich die Erweiterung nicht entgehen lassen. Cyberpunk bringt eine ganz besondere Stimmung auf den Bildschirm und beschäftigt mit seinen gesellschaftskritischen Themen und Zukunftsängsten nicht nur den gemeinen Gamer-Nerd. Als Open-World schafft CD Red hier eine Lebendige und sehr atmosphärische Großstadt zu erschaffen, die nicht immer echt wirkt aber sehr wohl dynamisch, lebendig und durchdacht. Das Gameplay, allen voran der Kampf machen durchgehend Spaß und bieten (auf Wunsch) viel Abwechslung und Spielraum für Experimente. Technisch ist Cyberpunk auch heute nicht perfekt und zwingt die meisten Systeme auf Max-Settings immer noch in die Knie, dafür sieht es aber auch grandios aus, vor allem wenn es regnet und sich die bunten Neon-Lichter in den nassen, dreckigen Straßen von Night City spiegeln. Die gut geschriebenen Storys, Dialoge und Charaktere ziehen einen in die Welt und bleiben im Kopf. Viele Entscheidungen mit Konsequenz wirken sich auf eines von 7 verschiedene, stets traurigen Enden aus, so muss das sein.

Ich freue mich auf die Fortsetzung und hoffe dann darauf, dass wir nicht nur Night City sondern auch die Erde mal hinter uns lassen werden.

sinceramente esse jogo se redimiu depois do lançamento e ainda bem que joguei só depois dele ficar bom, porque PUTAQUIPARIIU QUE JOGO ABSURDO DE INCRIVEL, HISTORIA F0DA COM IMERSÃO TOTAL. 130 horas de pura lore dentro do universo do jogo, e é louco pensar que muita gente na epoca do lançamento não pode presenciar em como a historia é impactante por causa daqueles bugs...

A história é muito interessante, principalmente pela forma como apresenta uma distopia em que praticamente tudo pode ser comprado, vendido ou substituído, até partes do próprio corpo e, em certo sentido, a própria identidade. Night City é um lugar extremamente desigual, onde megacorporações controlam boa parte da sociedade, enquanto as pessoas comuns tentam sobreviver entre violência, pobreza, tecnologia e a promessa de uma vida melhor que quase nunca chega.
O mais interessante é que o jogo não trata esse mundo apenas como um cenário bonito. A cidade tem uma história própria, diferentes grupos, culturas, gangues e conflitos políticos e corporativos. Existe uma sensação constante de que Night City já estava ali antes de V chegar e continuará existindo depois que a história acabar. As propagandas absurdas, os implantes, as drogas, as corporações e até os pequenos diálogos espalhados pela cidade ajudam a construir essa sensação de uma sociedade completamente dominada pelo capitalismo e pela tecnologia.
A história também consegue explorar muito bem temas como identidade, liberdade, mortalidade e o que realmente significa continuar sendo você mesmo quando seu corpo e sua mente podem ser modificados. Johnny Silverhand funciona justamente como uma extensão desses temas, tornando a relação dele com V uma das partes mais interessantes da narrativa.
Uma coisa que me incomodou um pouco, porém, foi a sensação de que nossas decisões nem sempre têm o peso que parecem ter. Existem escolhas realmente importantes, que mudam personagens, missões e até determinados finais, mas a maioria acaba parecendo menos significativa do que o jogo faz parecer. Muitas vezes você escolhe uma resposta pensando que aquilo vai mudar completamente alguma situação e, no fim, a história simplesmente segue seu curso. Não chega a estragar a experiência, mas é frustrante porque Cyberpunk constrói tão bem a ideia de liberdade e escolha que você acaba esperando que suas decisões tenham consequências muito maiores.
Também é impossível falar de Cyberpunk sem mencionar o estado em que o jogo foi lançado e o quanto ele melhorou desde então. Hoje é uma experiência muito mais sólida, e, sinceramente, durante minha jogatina encontrei pouquíssimos bugs realmente relevantes. Os únicos que lembro foram alguns carros simplesmente aparecendo ou ficando presos no chão do mapa e personagens falando durante diálogos completamente parados, sem fazer nenhum movimento. Comparado ao caos que o jogo já foi, isso chega a ser quase parte da experiência.
No fim, Cyberpunk 2077 é um jogo que melhorou absurdamente com o tempo e que tem um dos mundos mais interessantes que já vi em um RPG. A história, a atmosfera e principalmente a construção de Night City fazem valer muito a pena mergulhar nessa distopia. Só fica aquela sensação de que, em um jogo sobre liberdade e escolhas, eu gostaria que o jogo tivesse tido um pouco mais de coragem para deixar minhas decisões realmente mudarem o mundo ao meu redor, mesmo que, ocasionalmente, um carro ainda decida nascer dentro do asfalto.

I'm frankly not sure how this game receives acclaim now despite it still being somewhat of a mess. Granted, most of the large issues such as crashes (Most of the time) or overall surface presentation have been resolved in due part to patches. However, I question whether or not this approach to game design is going to work out for studios when they can't even out develop a game from a decade ago or more. There are multiple arguments or conversations to be had about why the game shipped in such a state for the initial release, but it doesn't help everything has to be reworked and tacked on due to poor planning. Such additions don't feel natural personally and very awkward during a playthrough. 

I can at least praise the concept/art/music aspects of the game or even the general plot of the story, but interest just falls off for the story/gameplay so quickly after Act I. There's not really any captivating characters to keep interest for me personally besides Jackie and Johnny, but [spoiler] Jackie ceases to be after Act I [/spoiler] and Johnny is not well written or acted in my opinion. The spam of characters/quests contacting you as well doesn't do the game any justice either. It would at least hold up in some regard if it played like an RPG which might separate it from the mundane gameplay, but a lot of times you are forced into doing whatever the scenario wants you to do. 

An example would be getting into Clouds at the start of Act II looking for Evelyn. You can't bypass the receptionist in any way besides jacking in and creating a profile, despite there being another sole choice for the intellect skill right below it stating that's not safe. In almost any other RPG, there'd be bribe, intimidate, persuade, maybe flirt, or even just blow their brains out choices, but that doesn't exist here and barely is present in other missions. What's more ironic is that later a mission comes up where having somebody access your character's system proves to be fatal as a result of there being no choice to deny them doing so. Contrast this to Deus Ex: Human Revolution from 2011 where even just updating your character's system/augmentations due to a recall proves to be a problem later on in the story and the term RPG for this game become laughable.  

In short, while presentation is here, the gameplay and depth of an RPG isn't. You have a overall cool surface level world to shoot and drive in, but no place to really to immerse or build yourself in as your V. I've picked up this game three times now to try and really love it, but it's just not there. Would recommend any other RPG, even if some like New Vegas need a literal 20 mods just to tape the engine back together so it'll work.

This game is... pretty good! Its biggest strength is its setting. It's a joy to pop on the in-game radio and travel around Night City via a car or motorbike. 
Its second biggest strength is its premise. The idea of having the personality of a sh*thead has-been rockerboy stuck in your head after a merc mission goes awry is brilliant. 
This game had a pretty rough launch, but it seems like things have since been ironed out quite nicely, and in my experience the game was rather polished, with only a few janky moments here and there.
The main story was engaging, albeit a bit confusing. I rarely understood what was going on since the dialogue was full of techno-babble and references to various factions and individuals, but I enjoyed it anyway thanks to the vibes.
The core missions were fun. It felt satisfying to blast up enemies with a shotgun, pick them off with a sniper rifle, or slash them to bits with a katana. Sometimes, stealth was necessary as well - and this I found enjoyable too. The gameplay is fairly simple, but the moving story kept things feeling interesting, and the final act was fantastic. The boss fights, though few and far between, were exciting.
Some of the side missions are worthwhile characters-centric detours. Panam, River, Claire, Judy, Brendan and the Peralezes are some of the welcome personalities that populate the world, in addition to main-quest characters like Takemura and Jackie. But, the 'gigs' do expose the core gameplay as quite shallow when it comes down to it, and can be missed without losing much in my opinion. Options such as  quick-hacking and using smart weapons existed, but since the game never posed much of a challenge, these strategies did not ever feel necessary or worth exploring. The skill trees and cyber-ware provided a decent sense of progression, but mostly consisted of simple stat increases rather than providing interesting new abilities that affected gameplay.
Overall, I'd say this isn't a must-play, but might be worth picking up if it's on sale and the trailers intrigues you.

Zerei Cyberpunk 2077 no lançamento e, naquela época, não recomendaria. Rejoguei diversas vezes ao longo dos anos, acompanhei a evolução e comprei até no Xbox. Hoje eu digo com tranquilidade: esse jogo É FODA. E Phantom Liberty é, pra mim, uma das melhores DLCs já feitas para qualquer jogo.

Essa mudança de opinião importa. Eu estava lá quando saiu, joguei até o fim e sei o quanto a recomendação mudou pra mim. Os problemas do lançamento continuam fazendo parte da história. Só que também seria injusto ignorar tudo que veio depois, principalmente tendo voltado tantas vezes a Night City.

A cidade continua sendo um dos grandes motivos pra entrar nesse mundo. Prédios empilhados, propaganda invadindo cada espaço e luxo dividindo a rua com miséria. A arquitetura conta muita coisa antes de alguém abrir a boca: quem tem dinheiro ocupa o espaço de um jeito, quem precisa sobreviver se aperta onde dá. Até o teu corpo entra nessa lógica de comprar uma versão melhor de si mesmo.

A história de V dá uma dimensão pessoal a esse cenário. Tem ambição, identidade, medo de morrer e aquela convivência com Johnny Silverhand, que consegue transformar um minuto de silêncio numa discussão. Os personagens ajudam a dar peso ao que está acontecendo. É muito mais fácil se importar com uma cidade quando tu se importa com quem vive nela.

E o combate tem liberdade pra sustentar as voltas. Armas, lâminas, furtividade e invasões rápidas mudam a maneira de abordar uma situação. Controlar câmeras e atacar pela rede exige uma preparação diferente de entrar cortando todo mundo. Montar a combinação de habilidades e implantes faz parte da graça, porque ela aparece na maneira como o personagem se movimenta e resolve os confrontos.

A atualização gratuita 2.0 reformulou vantagens, implantes e polícia. A armadura passou a depender principalmente dos implantes, com uma capacidade que limita o que tu consegue instalar. Essas mudanças são do jogo base. Phantom Liberty acrescenta sua própria campanha, Dogtown e a árvore Relic, entre outras novidades. Vale separar as duas coisas pra entender o tamanho da evolução.

Phantom Liberty merece espaço de verdade nesta análise. Dogtown tem uma identidade própria dentro de Night City, com estruturas arruinadas e uma milícia controlando o território. A trama de espionagem coloca V no meio de interesses políticos e lealdades difíceis de decifrar. Reed e Songbird fazem parte desse jogo em que confiar em alguém pode custar caro. A busca por uma saída continua pessoal, mesmo quando tem gente muito poderosa puxando os fios.

É uma expansão que eu coloco entre as melhores de qualquer jogo, sem precisar diminuir esse elogio. A história e os conflitos ampliam o que Cyberpunk tem de mais interessante: pessoas tentando conservar alguma liberdade num mundo que trata todo mundo como recurso. Pra quem gostou do jogo base, recomendo muito incluir Phantom Liberty na experiência.

Ainda existem limites. As origens de V poderiam influenciar mais a campanha, há atividades repetitivas e nem toda a cidade permite a interação que o cenário sugere. Isso não mudou o quanto gosto do conjunto hoje. Minha recomendação vem dessa relação de anos com a obra, passando pelo lançamento, pelas rejogadas e pela expansão.

9/10. Recomendo muito.

Comecei sem conseguir recomendar e terminei comprando de novo em outra plataforma. Night City levou meu dinheiro duas vezes, e eu ainda estou aqui elogiando.

Cyberpunk 2077 is nothing short of a monumental achievement in modern gaming. Its meticulously crafted open world, breathtaking visual fidelity, and extraordinarily immersive atmosphere set a benchmark that few titles can even aspire to reach. Night City is not merely a backdrop for the narrative; it is a living, breathing metropolis, teeming with moral ambiguity, social stratification, technological obsession, and the haunting consequences of unchecked corporate power.

What truly distinguishes the game, however, is its narrative sophistication. Beneath its dazzling neon lights and futuristic spectacle lies a profoundly human story about identity, mortality, freedom, and the desperate pursuit of meaning in an increasingly dehumanised world. Its characters are remarkably nuanced, its dialogue often incisive, and its most emotionally resonant moments linger long after the credits roll.

Visually, Cyberpunk 2077 is nothing less than extraordinary. The interplay of neon illumination, atmospheric fog, intricate environmental detail, and sophisticated lighting techniques creates an aesthetic that is simultaneously mesmerising and unsettling. Night City feels as though it has been ripped from the darkest, most compelling visions of the future and brought to life with astonishing technical precision.

Ultimately, Cyberpunk 2077 transcends the boundaries of conventional entertainment. It is an ambitious, thought-provoking, and occasionally heartbreaking exploration of what it means to remain human in a world that increasingly treats humanity as a commodity. Few games manage to combine such artistic ambition, narrative depth, and technological brilliance so convincingly. Cyberpunk 2077 is not merely a game worth experiencing; it is an experience that exemplifies the extraordinary artistic potential of the medium itself.

When you add mods into the mix, you're in a whole other beast of a game. 

Vanilla? The game shines brighter than any star in this sea of clouds. 
If you like games such as Fallout or Baldur's Gate, I'd highly recommend throwing this into your rotation.

Cyberpunk 2077 – En 2026 je le considère enfin “terminé” 🔥

Évaluation : ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

J’ai fait Cyberpunk 2077 dans son état actuel (mise à jour 2.0 + Phantom Liberty) et honnêtement, là je le vois enfin comme un jeu complet. Night City est devenue une ville où j’ai juste envie de me balader, le système de talents et d’implants a enfin du sens, et l’extension Phantom Liberty rajoute une histoire qui tient largement la route à côté de la campagne principale.

🌃 Night City donne vraiment envie d’y vivre (ou d’y mourir)
Aujourd’hui, la ville est juste incroyable à parcourir : chaque quartier a sa propre ambiance, les néons, la pluie, le bruit, les PNJ qui réagissent mieux… Tu peux passer ton temps à marcher, conduire ou rouler à moto juste pour admirer la ville, sans même suivre une mission. Les avis récents disent la même chose : visuellement et en termes d’ambiance, le jeu est enfin au niveau de ce qui était promis.

🦾 Le système 2.0 change tout
Avec la mise à jour 2.0, ils ont refait tout le système de compétences et de cyberware, et ça se sent direct. Au lieu d’avoir des petits bonus de +1% inutiles, tu débloques de vraies capacités qui changent ta manière de jouer : tu peux te construire un V netrunner, bourrin, ninja, hyper mobile, etc. Les combats sont bien plus dynamiques et agréables qu’à la sortie, et les armes ont enfin une vraie sensation de puissance.

🕵️ Phantom Liberty : le gros morceau qui manquait
Phantom Liberty, pour moi, c’est l’extension qui “termine” le jeu. Dogtown a une ambiance à part, plus fermée, plus oppressante, avec un côté espionnage / complot politique qui fonctionne super bien. Les nouveaux personnages (Songbird, Reed…) sont vraiment marquants, les missions sont très bien mises en scène, et le scénario tient largement le niveau de l’histoire principale, voire la dépasse par moments. Les tests et avis vont tous dans ce sens : c’est une extension dense, soignée, et pas juste quelques quêtes en plus.

🎭 Histoire, choix et personnages
Entre l’arc principal de V + Johnny et tout ce que rajoute Phantom Liberty, j’ai vraiment accroché aux personnages. Les dialogues sont bien écrits, les choix donnent vraiment l’impression d’avoir du poids, et certaines fins (surtout avec le contenu de Phantom Liberty) restent en tête longtemps après. Plusieurs critiques récentes parlent d’un jeu qui, narrativement, est enfin au niveau d’un grand RPG solo, et je suis clairement d’accord.

⚙️ Les défauts qui restent (mais qui ne gâchent pas tout)
Même en étant très positif, je peux admettre quelques points :

l’open world reste parfois un peu “guidé” : on va souvent de point A à point B pour lancer les meilleures quêtes,
​

il reste encore quelques bugs mineurs (animations, petites erreurs visuelles), même si rien à voir avec la sortie,

le jeu reste gourmand : pour vraiment profiter des graphismes et du ray tracing, il faut une bonne machine.

Mais dans mon cas, ça n’a jamais suffi à casser l’expérience.

💭 Mon ressenti global
En version 2.0 avec Phantom Liberty, Cyberpunk 2077 est enfin devenu le gros jeu solo que j’attendais au départ. Night City est hypnotisante, le système de progression est intéressant, les combats sont fun, et l’histoire (jeu de base + extension) m’a vraiment tenu accroché du début à la fin.

Du coup, maintenant que j’y ai joué dans ces conditions, je le mets clairement dans la catégorie “gros coup de cœur solo”. Si tu le découvres maintenant, tu joues à la meilleure version possible, pas à celle du lancement.

Faire une review objective après 200h de jeu c'est mission impossible, mais laissez moi vous donner les raisons qui font que je trouve ce jeu aussi bon.
Si vous connaissez Cyberpunk 2077 de nom, il y a de grandes chances que ce soit par sa sortie catastrophiquement buggée en 2020. Et bien le jeu de 2026 n'a plus rien à voir et mérite amplement sa place parmi les plus grands RPG de l'histoire. Il n'est pas exempt de bugs, mais ils sont devenus tellement anecdotiques et n'entachent en rien la qualité du jeu.

Pour commencer, le monde est immersif et incroyablement bien construit. La ville déjà : selon moi la qualité d'un open-world se mesure à "à quel point on est tenté d'utiliser la navigation rapide ?". Dans Cyberpunk 2077, la complexité, la variété et la beauté de la ville rend tout trajet largement préférable à une téléportation. Pourquoi devrais-je me rendre instantanément à l'autre bout de la ville lorsque je peux en profiter pour passer une quinzième fois dans ce quartier magnifique et riche en détails ? Le monde ensuite : le récit d'anticipation est splendide, réaliste et très immersif. L'existence d'une réalité alternative où l'Amérique de 2077 ressemble au jeu m'est parfaitement envisageable.

La qualité d'écriture de l'histoire et des personnages également. Jamais un dialogue ne m'a paru forcé, jamais un personnage ne m'a paru plat ou caricatural, jamais un moment de l'histoire ne m'a déçu. Souvent tragique, toujours incroyable à découvrir, le récit du jeu est honnêtement proche de la perfection. On reconnait bien la grande force de CD Projekt Red, déjà bien remarquable dans leur autre chef d'œuvre qu'est The Witcher 3. Idem pour le DLC Phantom Liberty : décidément ce studio aime faire des extensions à l'histoire encore plus incroyable que celle de leur jeu (déjà folle). Johnny, Panam, Judy, So Mi, Jackie : je ne vous oublierais jamais.

Dernier point et après promis j'arrête : la qualité folle de la personnalisation du gameplay. L'arbre de compétences offre tellement de façons de jouer c'est fou. Vous êtes fan du rentre-dedans et adorez charcuter les ennemis au corps à corps ? Vous avez une bonne dizaine d'options qui s'offrent à vous. Vous préférez l'infiltration précise et méticuleuse ? Une dizaine d'autres façons d'approcher chaque mission est possible. Ajoutez à cela la modification du corps, des vêtements, des véhicules et bien sûr les choix de dialogues et vous obtenez un niveau de personnalisation difficile à dépasser.

Mention honorable à la musique que j'écoute avec plaisir aussi bien en jeu qu'en dehors.

Cyberpunk 2077 is a highly controversial blockbuster that stumbled out of the gate but made a stunning comeback later. After multiple updates and the release of its DLC Phantom Liberty, it has evolved into a benchmark for cyberpunk-themed games, ideal for story-driven players and world-building enthusiasts.
 
Core Highlights
 
- Immersive Worldbuilding: The neon-lit streets, cybernetic enhancements, and holographic advertisements of Night City create a top-tier cyberpunk atmosphere, with exceptionally high-quality Chinese voice acting that takes immersion to the next level.

- Compelling Narrative & Characters: The symbiotic consciousness struggle between V and Johnny Silverhand is intensely gripping. Multiple endings are influenced by side quests, with key side stories featuring rich plots and movie-grade cutscenes.

- Revamped Gameplay & Updates: The 2.0 update overhauled skills, cyberware, and combat, enabling diverse playstyles (hacker, stealth, melee, etc.). The DLC Phantom Liberty boasts outstanding quality, with significantly improved optimization.

- Stunning Visuals & Music: Enhanced by ray tracing, the game delivers breathtaking graphics, especially shining in rainy nights and nightclub lighting effects. The electronic soundtrack perfectly fits the setting, amplifying the immersive experience.
 
Key Shortcomings
 
- Sense of Content Incompleteness: The main storyline is relatively short, with a large number of "cookie-cutter" gigs padding the open world, and some area designs failing to reach their full potential.

- Lack of Combat Depth: Once players master their preferred playstyle in the late game, combat becomes overly easy; AI and stealth mechanics are relatively simplistic, leading to a drop in challenge.

- Lingering Legacy Issues: Despite fixes for the disastrous bugs and poor optimization at launch, minor glitches still persist. Some systems (such as the police mechanism) remain poorly designed.

Despite the heavy initial refunds back at launch, this 2020 game turned massive profits, easily recouped its huge $300M+ budget, and reached 40 million copies sold worldwide—making it one of the best-selling RPGs of all time.

When a game's world-building, writing, and gameplay loop line up this well, I can completely see why. The game is so fantastic—it hits that sweet spot where you just want to wander around soaking in the atmosphere, explore Night City's side stories or side quests, or just to test out new iconic weapon builds on some NCPD targets. It makes every penny spent feel completely justified and keeps you coming back for "one more gig."

Iconic weapon? How does a shotgun that fires 8 target-seeking mini-explosive missiles—complete with screen-filling explosions—sound to you? Or how about a chatty AI pistol, or a machine gun spewing abusive remarks?

Even if there are still a few very minor bugs, they don't take away from the experience at all.

Nothing—no game—matches the rush of storming Dogtown's Barghest stronghold as V and causing absolute chaos: downing 50+ Barghest militias, pummeling those red-and-black heavy enforcers with the crazy AF Sasquatch’s Hammer alongside MaxTac AV drops, and rampaging through MaxTac until the latter calls in a second anti-cyberpsycho squad and you, V—that freak-of-nature cyberpsycho alpha maniac—are forced to scramble for cover.

With so many branching endings, almost every path leaves you with a lingering sense of loss, quiet existential dread, or bittersweet acceptance. It's a staple of the cyberpunk genre: there's no such thing as a 100% happy ending — you just can't win it all.

And one of the best parts? It still works on an old ROG GL753VE with a GTX 1050 Ti mobile from 2017, hitting 70 FPS on medium settings!

The game is still so average all this time later.

Even with heavy modding, the game just feels so dead. Story is pretty average, and there's still so many bugs after all this time. It's also crazy that there are just so many low quality/missing features. GTA Online had callable cars that actually drove to you on release, whereas even after however many years, Cyberpunk's best effort is "spawn it instantly behind you and sometimes it won't glitch out".

An example of the poor story writing is Jackie: gets introduced, doesn't mind that you "ruined" a massive heist, suddenly best friends, "fast forward 4 months" trope, do one job, anti climactic death. Builds literally zero attachment to the character that's supposed to be your best friend, and kills him off immediately.

And the AI car guy: why tf would an AI car be doing you favours? The whole point of an AI is that it's supposed to be cold and efficient, which is what they paint it out to be when it's introduced. "No I can't deviate from the route, blah blah blah", 2 minutes later, "yes, I can go out of my way to come out of the city where I explicitly don't operate without guarantee of payment, that makes sense for a sophisticated AI with no connection to your character".

There is no sense of scale in the game, because the area design is so bad. The main city itself is pretty tiny for a AAA game, especially when so much of it is just empty filler. I was expecting to be wowed with a massive futuristic city that felt alive, but it's the complete opposite. You can really tell it's very much a patch job from the botched release, as still nothing that they promised before release is actually possible with exploration.

L'un des jeux les plus immersifs auquel j'ai pu jouer de toute ma vie, si ce n'est le plus.

J'ai eu la chance de découvrir ce jeu après sa grosse mise à jour 2.0, qui retravaillait drastiquement tous les points du jeux, qui étaient, qu'on se le dise, à chier pendant ses premières années de sa sortie.
CDPR à su remonter la pente et nous pondre une mise à jour qui a transformé une beine à ordure en un pur chef d'oeuvre.

Cyberpunk n'est pas juste un jeu RPG futuriste avec des gadjets tah robocop, non, c'est vraiment un simulateur de mercenaire du futur. On ne joue pas un personnage lambda dans une ville quelconque à essayer de se faire des sous, on joue notre histoire. Alors certes, le jeu vous prends beaucoup par la main mais quand je jouais au jeu, je m'isolais de tout pour être à 100% en immersion dans le jeu... et bordel de merde, que c'était intense.

Que ça soit l'ambiance et la vie qui regorge les rues de Night City et ses alentours, ses graphismes bluffants (Raytracing MAGNIFIQUE), son sound design aux petits ognons et bien évidemment Elias Changuel qui donne sa voix au personnage principal en VF, ou bien Jean Pierre Michael (vf de brad pitt) pour la voix de Johnny, on ne peut que jouir de la beauté de ce jeu.

Pendant longtemps Skyrim était mon jeu préféré, mais aujourd'hui.. a mal vieillit (ok y'a les mods mais installer 300Go de mods pour avoir un jeu moderne, on souffle). Devant cyberpunk j'ai pleuré, j'ai ri, j'ai été surpris, j'ai eu peur par moments, et je me suis même attaché aux personnages du jeu (alors que ça m'arrive très rarement).

游戏一定要说说游戏性，到了2.31版本游戏各方面平衡和bug已经少了太多，但是还是有些硬伤，首先是没有多人模式，这点对于一个3A游戏来说是个遗憾，没有多人游戏，主线剧情如此之短让很多预购玩家感到不值得。第二个就是这游戏的载具驾驶模式手感太差了，而且到了2077年你还弄什么地铁和汽车？浮空车应该是出门标配才对，要么你开，要么你打的，搞得跟2020一样。第三点就是游戏想象力不够足，除了刚才的载具模式，还有很多很多细节可以想象，任务模式可以创新，但是制作组离开了巫师想象不出了。最后说说武器系统，武器系统我始终弄不明白，普通武器无法升级，不朽武器没有插件，插件不能更换，让我说的话，未来的枪是不是V应该带3把，然后改装一些功能，你弄了几百个格子，V带的了那么多么枪和刀，事实上也不需要，服装也是，这一点我不知道制作组怎么想的。战斗系统虽然开放，但是整体令人不是很舒服，潜入和战斗是不是要有一个明确的界限呢，比如某些任务就是要完全意义潜入，失败了就结束了，有些明确强攻，干他多少人，有些测试是不是要一些特殊的条件，比如车辆比如魔蝎等等。
音乐，是这部游戏最亮的点，尤其是往日之影里面的那段演出，简直就是一个超梦演唱会。但是没有好的剧情和优化，音乐不足以撑得起场面。
总体上来看，2.31版本的2077和往日之影是可玩的，尤其是对一个喜欢科幻、未来或赛博朋克类型的玩家来说，是可以体验的，但是不建议平价入手，还是等等打折吧。

Cyberpunk 2077 is not the best game ever made, but what it does well, it does at an exceptionally high level. The game is wrapped in the stunning setting of Night City, a visually breathtaking metropolis filled with vibrant colors, towering architecture, and dense urban design. However, despite its visual richness, the world can sometimes feel oddly hollow, lacking a stronger sense of interactivity or the feeling that the player can truly live in it.

From a gameplay perspective, Cyberpunk 2077 offers a solid and flexible experience. It provides a high degree of player agency, allowing different playstyles through varied builds, approaches to combat, and decision-making. Whether you prefer stealth, hacking, or direct combat, the game supports meaningful experimentation, which significantly enhances replayability.

Where the game truly excels is in its characters and storytelling. CD Projekt Red once again demonstrates its strength in narrative design, delivering both main and side quests that are consistently engaging from beginning to end. The writing, performances, and emotional weight of character-driven moments stand out as some of the strongest aspects of the experience. This is even more evident in the Phantom Liberty expansion, where the overall narrative, pacing, and gameplay loop feel more refined and cohesive than in the base game. The expansion elevates the experience and showcases what the game is capable of at its best.

Visually, the game is outstanding. The graphical fidelity, detailed environments, and high-quality animations contribute to an immersive presentation. Lighting plays a crucial role, with neon reflections and ray tracing pushing the atmosphere to another level, especially in night-time scenes where the city truly comes alive.

Overall, Cyberpunk 2077 delivers a strong and memorable experience. Despite some shortcomings in world interactivity, it stands out thanks to its excellent storytelling, compelling characters, impressive visuals, and outstanding soundtrack. It is a game well worth playing, particularly for those who appreciate narrative-driven RPGs.
