Гигачады устраивают великую пиарную кампанию по кп: разочарование, тонны критики, вовзрат средств, кредит доверия в минус. Спустя пару лет - великая история, великие персонажи, ну и в общем все то что было у Геральта в его старые годы. Вот только вернуть доверие оказалось сложнее, чем с трилогией про темное фэнтези, ибо тогда гигачады смахивали скорее на инцелов, чье видение и подход к созданию игр заметили полмира, для коего 3 часть считается чуть ли не лучшей игрой за все время. Философские взгляды, хорошо прописанные персонажи, ОСОБЕННО лорная составляющая мира, одержимость зацепиться за последний вагон, дабы не умереть, очень легко передаваемая человеку за монитором, управляющему гг, классные механики игры и различные способы пройти тот или иной квест не смогли повлиять на аудиторию, когда у нее ломаются скрипты и им приходится заново перепроходить все с последнего сейва. Да, качество при выходе было мягко говоря неиграбельное, и эта тенденция переносить и исправлять уже ГОТОВЫЙ продукт, за который платят деньги люди - хуйня откровенно говоря, но что поделать. Исправили. Выкатили DLC, которое ну ахереть как расширяет и без того большую вселенную, добавляя вариации в конечном исходе (самую реалистичную, имхо), пусть и не до конца, но хотя бы всего того, за что корили CD project уже нет. Хорошая игра предлагает кайфануть от ее прохождения, отличная игра заставляет задуматься, а в киберпанке во время его прохождения приходится каждые полчаса ставить на паузу и выходить выкуривать по 3 сигареты, дабы не впасть в глубокие раздумья и попытаться оставить их в игре. Кому-то сеттинг вайбует, кому-то история, а я до сих пор чувствую, как меня заебал этот город, отдаю гитару пацаненку с улицы, надеваю темные очки и объявляю, что мои выступления закончены. Навсегда

Eu comprei Cyberpunk 2077 na pré-venda lá na Epic. Na época eu tava muito hypado, acompanhando trailer, promessa, Night City brilhando como se fosse o futuro que todo mundo queria viver. Aí o jogo saiu… e todo mundo sabe o que aconteceu. Bugs, problemas, decepção. Foi estranho ver algo que parecia tão grande tropeçar daquele jeito.
Mesmo assim eu nunca consegui simplesmente odiar esse jogo.
Anos depois eu comprei ele de novo na Steam. Não porque eu precisava… mas porque eu queria voltar. Queria ver se aquele sentimento ainda estava lá, e estava.
Cyberpunk 2077 é um jogo sobre um mundo quebrado, mas também sobre pessoas tentando existir dentro dele. Night City é linda, mas é uma beleza triste. Tudo brilha, mas nada realmente vive. É uma cidade cheia de luz neon tentando esconder o vazio por trás.
E de certa forma… jogar isso dá uma sensação meio melancólica.
Porque o jogo fala muito sobre tempo, identidade e mortalidade. Sobre como a gente tenta deixar alguma marca no mundo, mesmo sabendo que talvez tudo desapareça. É uma história sobre aceitar o inevitável e ainda assim continuar andando.
Com o tempo, patches e atualizações, o jogo foi se reconstruindo. É quase poético pensar nisso. Um jogo sobre redenção… que também precisou se redimir.
Hoje ele não é só um RPG de mundo aberto.
Pra mim ele virou um sentimento.
A trilha sonora tocando enquanto você anda sozinho por Night City à noite, as conversas estranhas, os personagens quebrados tentando encontrar algum significado… tudo isso cria uma experiência que fica com você depois que o jogo acaba.
Nem todo jogo precisa ser perfeito.
Alguns só precisam fazer você sentir alguma coisa.
E Cyberpunk 2077 conseguiu isso comigo.

Night Cityde neredeyse görebileceğim her şeyi gördüm, bütün sonlara gittim, yan görevlerin peşinden koştum ve farklı seçimlerin nereye çıktığını merak edip tekrar tekrar oynadım. Sonra bir de modlarla oynayıp oyunu iyice kendi kafama göre değiştirdim. Oyunun en sevdiğim tarafı kesinlikle Night Citynin kendisi. Şehir sadece görevden göreve giderken aradan geçtiğin bir yer gibi hissettirmiyor. Bazen hiçbir şey yapmadan arabaya binip sokaklarda dolaşmak bile yetiyor. Neon ışıklar, yağmur, radyolar, insanların konuşmaları, sokakta yaşanan küçük olaylar ve her yerde gördüğün farklı insanlar şehri gerçekten canlı hissettiriyor. Özellikle gece yağmur yağarken arabayla şehirde dolaşmanın bende ayrı bir yeri var. Bazen görev bile yapmadan yarım saat sadece şehirde gezdiğim oldu. Müzikler de bu atmosferin çok büyük bir parçası. Oyunun soundtracki ve radyolardaki parçalar hala ara sıra açıp dinlediğim şeyler. Bazı parçaları duyduğumda direkt Night City aklıma geliyor. Ana tema müzikleri, görevlerde çalan parçalar, boss karşılaşmalarındaki müzikler ve radyoların genel seçimi oyunun atmosferini inanılmaz tamamlıyor. Oyunu kapattıktan sonra bile bazı müzikleri dinlemeye devam ettiğim çok oldu.

Hikaye tarafında özellikle yan görevleri çok seviyorum. Ana hikayenin yanında bazı karakterlerin hikayeleri öyle güzel yazılmış ki ana görevlerden daha fazla aklımda kalan anlar oldu. Johnny Silverhand burada ayrı bir konu zaten. Başta sadece sürekli başına bela olan bir karakter gibi görünürken zamanla Vnin hikayesinin en önemli parçalarından birine dönüşüyor. Johnnynin sürekli bir anda ortaya çıkması, yorum yapması, olaylara kendi kafasına göre karışması ve V ile olan atışmaları oyuna çok farklı bir hava katıyor. Mizahı da çok hoşuma gidiyor. Bazen ciddi bir sahnenin ortasında Johnny gelip öyle bir şey söylüyor ki insanın bütün havası değişiyor. Keanu Reevesin performansı da karakteri akılda kalıcı yapan şeylerden biri bence. Panam, Judy, Kerry, River ve diğer karakterler de Vnin hikayesini sadece ana senaryodan ibaret olmaktan çıkarıyor. Özellikle bazı yan görevlerin sonunda karakterlerle kurduğun bağ ana hikayedeki bazı olaylardan daha fazla aklımda kaldı. Oyunun en güzel yaptığı şeylerden biri de Night Cityde yaşayan insanların sadece görev vermek için orada olmadığını hissettirmesi.

Rol yapma tarafına gelirsek burada oyunu biraz daha farklı görüyorum. Üst düzey bir RPG olduğunu söylemem ama kesinlikle zayıf da değil. Farklı seçimler yapmak ve farklı sonlara ulaşmak güzel ama bazı görevlerde keşke seçimlerimiz ve geliştirdiğimiz karakter daha fazla etkili olsaydı dediğim çok oldu. Özellikle bazı konuşmalarda sahip olduğun skill veya attribute yüksek olsa bile konuşmanın sonucunun pek değişmediği durumlar var. Bazı görevlerde belirli bir build yapmış olmanın veya belli bir özelliğe yatırım vermenin daha fazla karşılığını görmek isterdim. Yani oyun sana rol yapma özgürlüğü veriyor ama bunu her zaman sonuna kadar kullanmıyor. Buna rağmen build sistemi oyunu tekrar tekrar oynatıyor. Bir oyunda gizlilik ve quickhacklerle ilerlerken başka bir oyunda katanayla ortalığı dağıtmak, başka bir oyunda tabanca ve kritik vuruşlara ağırlık vermek baya farklı hissettirebiliyor. Aynı göreve farklı bir karakterle girince bile yaklaşımın değişiyor. Modlarla beraber bu tarafı benim için daha da genişledi. Bir noktadan sonra oyunu kendi istediğim Cyberpunk deneyimine çevirmeye başladım. Ama buglardan da bahsetmemek olmaz. Oyun bugün geldiği noktada eskisine göre çok daha iyi olsa da arada hala saç baş yolduran şeyler çıkabiliyor. Intercom açılmıyor, bir görevde olması gereken şey düzgün tetiklenmiyor, araba bir anda patlıyor, NPC veya araçlar spawnlanırken saçma sapan şeyler olabiliyor. Bazen de hiçbir anlamı olmayan küçük animasyon veya fizik hataları çıkıyor karşına. Özellikle yüzlerce saat oynayınca bunların hepsini görüyorsun. Bazıları komik oluyor ama bazıları da tam önemli bir görev sırasında çıkınca insanın bütün atmosferini bozuyor. Yine de oyunun bütün bu kusurlarına rağmen Night Citynin içine geri dönmek istemem benim için çok şey anlatıyor. Çünkü bir oyunda yüzlerce saat geçirip bütün sonları görüp yan görevleri bitirip farklı buildler deneyip üstüne modlarla tekrar oynadıktan sonra hala şehre dönmek istiyorsam orada gerçekten sevdiğim bir şey var demektir.

Phantom Liberty de bence oyunun en önemli parçalarından biri. DLCnin hikayesi, karakterleri ve özellikle Dogtownun atmosferi ana oyundan farklı bir tat veriyor. Daha kapalı ve daha yoğun bir bölgede geçmesi hoşuma gitti. Songbird, Reed ve diğer karakterlerle olan ilişkiler ve verdiğin kararların seni farklı noktalara götürmesi DLCyi sadece yeni görevler eklenmiş bir paket gibi hissettirmiyor. Hikayenin bazı yerlerinde gerçekten ne yapacağına karar vermekte zorlandığın anlar oluyor. Özellikle sonlara doğru olayların aldığı yön ve bazı seçimlerin sonuçları baya akılda kalıcı. Phantom Liberty aynı zamanda oyunun zaten güçlü olan atmosferini başka bir tarafa taşıyor. Dogtownun kendine has yapısı, karakterleri ve hikayesi Night Citynin geri kalanından ayrılıyor ama yine de oyunun dünyasına ait hissettiriyor. Ana oyunu seven biri için DLCnin hikayeye ve oynanışa yaptığı katkıyı görmezden gelmek mümkün değil.

Cyberpunk 2077 benim için kusursuz bir oyun değil. RPG tarafında daha fazla özgürlük verebilirdi, bazı seçimlerin etkisi daha büyük olabilirdi ve buglar hala zaman zaman karşıma çıkıyor. Ama bunların yanında Night City, karakterler, yan görevler, Johnny Silverhand, müzikler, atmosfer, build çeşitliliği ve farklı sonlar için tekrar oynama isteği o kadar güçlü ki bütün bunlar bir şekilde ağır basıyor.

隠しルート含め全ED達成。（青アイコン依頼をあと10個ほど未着手のみ）
遊びやすいが、人を選ぶ部分も多い。しかし素晴らしい作品だったと思います。そんな作品でした。

・バグについて

昔は酷かったらしいので、バグの存在が気になる方もいると思いますが、ここまで遊んで進行形の不具合は一度も起こっていません。しゃがんでいるはずの人が立ってしまっていたり…といった見た目の多少の問題がまだちょいちょいあります。が、起きるバグはすべてその程度。それも150時間遊んで10回もなかった程度です。

・アクション難易度について

難易度ですが、近接脳筋プレイでやっていましたが、FPSほぼ未経験の自分でも難易度はそこまで高くない感じでした。最初はハードで開始し、プレイ時間50を過ぎてからはベリーハード固定。それでも一番手こずったのはジャッキーと潜入するいちばん初期のクエスト（ハード）でした。それに比べれば、難しいとされているジョニーと二人だけでアラサカ陥落させる隠しルートのラストの戦闘（ベリーハード）のほうが遥かに楽です。

つまりこのゲームはアクションとしては序盤ほどきつく、その後はきちんとVを成長させていけばどんどん楽になるという仕様。序盤で詰まっている人はキツイのはそこだけなので諦めないで。総合的な難易度としては低めです。

・ストーリーについて

一つ一つのストーリーはハードで、救いがないものが多いです。常に何かを得るためには何かを失う必要がある。ナイトシティはそんな現実を突きつけてくる。一方でそんな世界を必死に生きるVの人生はまさに充実している。Vのハードな人生は顛末であるEDまで続きます。これが映画だったら苦しいだけの作品ですが、この作品の真の目的はそんな体験を通じて「人は何のためにどう生きるか」を問いかける事にあるようです。

素晴らしい話だった…と、思うかどうかは人によりけりですが、きっとあなたの記憶には深く刻まれる体験となるハズです。ぜひプレイしてみてください。

Cyberpunk 2077 çıkış gününde yaşanan rezaletten sonra ayağa kalkıp “ben buradayım” demeyi başaran nadir oyunlardan biri. Evet, ilk hâlini oynayan herkes travma yaşadı. Bug’lar, çökmeler, yarım hissi… Ama bugün geldiği noktaya bakınca şunu net söylüyorum: bu oyun artık bambaşka bir seviyede ve çıktığı hâliyle zerre alakası yok.

Şu an Cyberpunk 2077 inanılmaz derecede stabil. Bug neredeyse yok, performans tutarlı, sistemler çalışıyor. Oyun nihayet olması gereken hâline evrilmiş durumda. Ve en güzeli, bu sefer gerçekten oynadığını hissediyorsun; oyun seni yarıda bırakmıyor, sinir krizine sokmuyor. Yani evet, CDPR sıçtı ama sonra toparlayıp temizledi. Hakkını yemem.

Night City hâlâ sektördeki en iyi açık dünya şehirlerinden biri. Bu şehir sadece büyük değil, karakterli. Sokakta yürürken bile bir ağırlık var. Görsel tasarım, ışıklandırma, ses kullanımı… Hepsi seni içine çekiyor. Burası gezmelik bir harita değil, yaşanan bir yer. Oyunun atmosferi tek başına satıyor zaten.

Hikâye tarafı ise oyunun bel kemiği. V’nin yolculuğu, Johnny Silverhand ile olan çatışmalı ilişki, yan görevlerin beklenmedik derecede güçlü yazımı… Cyberpunk burada hiç şaka yapmıyor. Birçok yan görev ana hikâyeden daha etkili. Karakterler klişe değil, diyaloglar yapay durmuyor. Oyun sana duyguyu zorla dayatmıyor, yaşatıyor.

Oynanış da artık çok daha oturmuş durumda. Build çeşitliliği, silah hissi, siber yetenekler, stealth ve çatışma dengesi gayet sağlam. Eskiden “neden böyle” dediğin şeylerin çoğu ya düzeltilmiş ya da tamamen elden geçirilmiş. Şu hâliyle oyun akıyor, takılmadan oynatıyor ve tatmin ediyor.

Ve evet, şunu açık açık söyleyeyim: Ben bu oyunu gerçekten çok seviyorum. Sadece “düzeldiği için” değil, bugün sunduğu deneyim yüzünden. Cyberpunk 2077 şu an oynanması gereken, hatta kaçırılmaması gereken bir oyun. Çıkıştaki hâli yüzünden hâlâ önyargılı olanlar büyük resmi kaçırıyor.

Özetle:
Çıkışta rezalet.
Bugün tertemiz.
Atmosfer efsane.

Easiest 10/10

Reasons for it:
1) It scratches that cyberpunk itch deus ex hr,md left.
2) Story and characters are very well written.
3) Gameplay can be overwhemling at first but as you learn the mechanics and ease into it, Ideas start flowing in. The type of build you wanna run, freedom to do so is insane. 
4) Gunplay feels snappy and melee is just as satisfying.
5) Dialouges have a natural feel to them. And voice acting is some of the best I've seen in gaming.
6) Vehicle variety seems impressive. (although I haven't experienced much of this of gameplay yet)
7) It has solid replay values.
8) Characters so good, reminded me of OG bioware games such as mass effect and dragon age origins, where you'll actually care about them.
9) Visually this game is just breathtaking, all my settings are cranked to max except for RT and with hdr support. It really makes Night city feel alive and it's absolutely a visual delight.
10) CDPR wasn't kidding about the side content not being check-markers but actual content worth engaging with. 

Gripes
1) Even tho having many character customisation options there aren't many good hair styles for male V, if you just wanna go with the regular male V.
2) Haven't encountered major bugs but I did come across one where my car vanished and a dude clipped through a wall but at this point it is a funny occurence than a game- breaking experience.
3) Have to really hold back myself from using preem, choom and biz in my day to day lingo lol
4) Apart from one or two tracks so far in-game yet. The tracks haven't really hit it off yet. I wish i'll discover good music, cuz i see myself pouring more hours into the game.
5) Lastly, I feel I wish I came to this experience earlier. Just roaming in Night City lowers my stress levels.

What a ride. Didn't expect to be left questioning loyalty, survival, and how often “I’m trying to help you” means someones about to ruin your life.

After playing every ending, including Phantom Liberty, I changed my mind about some characters quite a few times. It went from understanding someone, to hating it, back to sympathize with them. The world and story excells in showing raw actions and consequences, while not judging directly anyone.

Major spoilers below. Seriously, play the game.

[spoiler]I won't go into the base game, as it allready aged and all loved and hated Johny, but he remained authentic.

Songbird was a tough one. I followed her path first, betrayed Reed, then spent half the journey wondering whether I backed the wrong person. She lied to everyone, to V, used his desperation to save herself. Meanwhile, Reed increasingly seemed like a man who genuinely wanted to get everyone out alive.

Fuck Myers btw. All that talk about duty and saving lives, while people become disposable the second they threaten her political interests. I wished I could have shot her the moment I met her.

I sent So Mi to the Moon first. Killing Reed didnt feel good. He believed in what he was doing, and I really hoped it would work out somehow. So I went back and handed her over. Reed alive, Alex alive, Songbird alive, yet back in FIA hands, but maybe Reed would help her. Seemed like a decent compromise.

Then I took the cure...
After spending the entire game looking for a way for V to survive, I finally got one. Two years in a coma, Johnny gone, Panam gone, almost nobody left. The life V fought so hard to keep had moved on without him. That fucking hurt and all of sudden those 6 uncertain months with people I cared about looked a lot more valuable than they had before.

The Arasaka ending had already left a rotten taste. I felt sorry for Goro, much like Reed: capable, loyal men who believe they’re doing the right thing, serving institutions that are perfectly happy to use them up. Even the rooftop suicide felt like it might spare everyone else until those calls showed what V would leave behind.

So I went back again. Betrayed Songbird in Firestarter. Watched everything fall apart. Alex died, So Mi lost control, and I started thinking she really was the root of the whole disaster.

Cynosure: that Cerberus sequence was fun and scary and I loved it. First time in a while that my V didnt feel like the overpowered killing machine.
Songbirds memories hit: before all this, she was basically a kid who wanted to become a great netrunner. Took a dangerous shot at a bigger life. Sound familiar?
But she didn't have V's luck to remain free for much longer, netwatch would have gotten her soon enough, so Reed thought recruiting her would save her.
Myers turned her into a weapon and kept pushing her into the Blackwall until she was losing herself. By the time she reaches V, Songbird doesn't trusted anyone, and tries anything for survival.
I know it doesn’t erase what she did, but I finally could see her perspective.

I played both outcomes in that bunker. After seeing everything, I came back to the Moon.

Save So Mi. Shoot Reed. Walk away from the FIA cure.

I still feel bad for Reed. Especially after seeing that he could begin questioning his loyalty for the F*ingIA in the other ending. I wished he could have reached that point before.
Also gave that medal to a begger, just like Songbird did.[/spoiler]

All in all it was a emotional roller coaster, absolutely fucking worth it.

So I will end with a quote from Johny:
"Swap meat for chrome, live a BD fantasy, whatever, but at the end of it all, it's the code you live by that defines who you are."

I don’t care what anyone says — [b]Cyberpunk 2077[/b] has come a long way. What started as a rough launch is now one of the most immersive, emotional, and downright beautiful open-world RPGs out there.

Night City feels alive — not just visually, but emotionally. You can walk down a random street and get lost in the atmosphere. The lighting, the music, the voices in the background — everything feels deliberate.

[b]The writing and characters?[/b] Incredible. V and Johnny Silverhand have some of the best chemistry I’ve ever seen in a game. Every major quest feels handcrafted, and even the smaller side jobs carry real emotional weight.

The [b]Phantom Liberty[/b] expansion took it all to another level. Idris Elba’s performance is top-tier, and the spy-thriller tone fits perfectly with the world’s darker side.

The gunplay and combat feel tight and weighty now. Cars actually drive properly, cops react like they should, and performance on PC is smooth. CDPR really pulled it together — it’s not just “fixed,” it’s reborn.

[hr]
[b]Pros:[/b]
[+] Deep, emotional storytelling
[+] Fantastic performances
[+] One of the most detailed open worlds ever made
[+] Great combat, driving, and stealth systems (post 2.0)
[+] Top-tier music and atmosphere

[b]Cons:[/b]
[–] Still the occasional bug or jank moment
[–] You’ll wish there was even more

[hr]
[b]Verdict:[/b]
Cyberpunk 2077 went from “what could’ve been” to “what games should strive to be.”
If you skipped it at launch — now’s the time.

Польские гигачады выпустили трилогию забагованного Ведьмака (+недавний ТАКЖЕ убитый производительностью ремастер трешки): великая РПГ (ага, да), великая история, великие персонажи, великая игра. Гигачады устраивают великую пиарную кампанию по кп: разочарование, тонны критики, вовзрат средств, кредит доверия в минус. Спустя пару лет - великая история, великие персонажи, ну и в общем все то что было у Геральта в его старые годы. Вот только вернуть доверие оказалось сложнее, чем с трилогией про темное фэнтези, ибо тогда гигачады смахивали скорее на инцелов, чье видение и подход к созданию игр заметили полмира, для коего 3 часть считается чуть ли не лучшей игрой за все время. Философские взгляды, хорошо прописанные персонажи, ОСОБЕННО лорная составляющая мира, одержимость зацепиться за последний вагон, дабы не умереть, очень легко передаваемая человеку за монитором, управляющему гг, классные механики игры и различные способы пройти тот или иной квест не смогли повлиять на аудиторию, когда у нее ломаются скрипты и им приходится заново перепроходить все с последнего сейва. Да, качество при выходе было мягко говоря неиграбельное, и эта тенденция переносить и исправлять уже ГОТОВЫЙ продукт, за который платят деньги люди - хуйня откровенно говоря, но что поделать. Исправили. Выкатили DLC, которое ну ахереть как расширяет и без того большую вселенную, добавляя вариации в конечном исходе (самую реалистичную, имхо), пусть и не до конца, но хотя бы всего того, за что корили CD project уже нет. Хорошая игра предлагает кайфануть от ее прохождения, отличная игра заставляет задуматься, а в киберпанке во время его прохождения приходится каждые полчаса ставить на паузу и выходить выкуривать по 3 сигареты, дабы не впасть в глубокие раздумья и попытаться оставить их в игре. Кому-то сеттинг вайбует, кому-то история, а я до сих пор чувствую, как меня заебал этот город, отдаю гитару пацаненку с улицы, надеваю темные очки и объявляю, что мои выступления закончены. Навсегда

Eu comprei Cyberpunk 2077 na pré-venda lá na Epic. Na época eu tava muito hypado, acompanhando trailer, promessa, Night City brilhando como se fosse o futuro que todo mundo queria viver. Aí o jogo saiu… e todo mundo sabe o que aconteceu. Bugs, problemas, decepção. Foi estranho ver algo que parecia tão grande tropeçar daquele jeito.
Mesmo assim eu nunca consegui simplesmente odiar esse jogo.
Anos depois eu comprei ele de novo na Steam. Não porque eu precisava… mas porque eu queria voltar. Queria ver se aquele sentimento ainda estava lá, e estava.
Cyberpunk 2077 é um jogo sobre um mundo quebrado, mas também sobre pessoas tentando existir dentro dele. Night City é linda, mas é uma beleza triste. Tudo brilha, mas nada realmente vive. É uma cidade cheia de luz neon tentando esconder o vazio por trás.
E de certa forma… jogar isso dá uma sensação meio melancólica.
Porque o jogo fala muito sobre tempo, identidade e mortalidade. Sobre como a gente tenta deixar alguma marca no mundo, mesmo sabendo que talvez tudo desapareça. É uma história sobre aceitar o inevitável e ainda assim continuar andando.
Com o tempo, patches e atualizações, o jogo foi se reconstruindo. É quase poético pensar nisso. Um jogo sobre redenção… que também precisou se redimir.
Hoje ele não é só um RPG de mundo aberto.
Pra mim ele virou um sentimento.
A trilha sonora tocando enquanto você anda sozinho por Night City à noite, as conversas estranhas, os personagens quebrados tentando encontrar algum significado… tudo isso cria uma experiência que fica com você depois que o jogo acaba.
Nem todo jogo precisa ser perfeito.
Alguns só precisam fazer você sentir alguma coisa.
E Cyberpunk 2077 conseguiu isso comigo.

Night Cityde neredeyse görebileceğim her şeyi gördüm, bütün sonlara gittim, yan görevlerin peşinden koştum ve farklı seçimlerin nereye çıktığını merak edip tekrar tekrar oynadım. Sonra bir de modlarla oynayıp oyunu iyice kendi kafama göre değiştirdim. Oyunun en sevdiğim tarafı kesinlikle Night Citynin kendisi. Şehir sadece görevden göreve giderken aradan geçtiğin bir yer gibi hissettirmiyor. Bazen hiçbir şey yapmadan arabaya binip sokaklarda dolaşmak bile yetiyor. Neon ışıklar, yağmur, radyolar, insanların konuşmaları, sokakta yaşanan küçük olaylar ve her yerde gördüğün farklı insanlar şehri gerçekten canlı hissettiriyor. Özellikle gece yağmur yağarken arabayla şehirde dolaşmanın bende ayrı bir yeri var. Bazen görev bile yapmadan yarım saat sadece şehirde gezdiğim oldu. Müzikler de bu atmosferin çok büyük bir parçası. Oyunun soundtracki ve radyolardaki parçalar hala ara sıra açıp dinlediğim şeyler. Bazı parçaları duyduğumda direkt Night City aklıma geliyor. Ana tema müzikleri, görevlerde çalan parçalar, boss karşılaşmalarındaki müzikler ve radyoların genel seçimi oyunun atmosferini inanılmaz tamamlıyor. Oyunu kapattıktan sonra bile bazı müzikleri dinlemeye devam ettiğim çok oldu.

Hikaye tarafında özellikle yan görevleri çok seviyorum. Ana hikayenin yanında bazı karakterlerin hikayeleri öyle güzel yazılmış ki ana görevlerden daha fazla aklımda kalan anlar oldu. Johnny Silverhand burada ayrı bir konu zaten. Başta sadece sürekli başına bela olan bir karakter gibi görünürken zamanla Vnin hikayesinin en önemli parçalarından birine dönüşüyor. Johnnynin sürekli bir anda ortaya çıkması, yorum yapması, olaylara kendi kafasına göre karışması ve V ile olan atışmaları oyuna çok farklı bir hava katıyor. Mizahı da çok hoşuma gidiyor. Bazen ciddi bir sahnenin ortasında Johnny gelip öyle bir şey söylüyor ki insanın bütün havası değişiyor. Keanu Reevesin performansı da karakteri akılda kalıcı yapan şeylerden biri bence. Panam, Judy, Kerry, River ve diğer karakterler de Vnin hikayesini sadece ana senaryodan ibaret olmaktan çıkarıyor. Özellikle bazı yan görevlerin sonunda karakterlerle kurduğun bağ ana hikayedeki bazı olaylardan daha fazla aklımda kaldı. Oyunun en güzel yaptığı şeylerden biri de Night Cityde yaşayan insanların sadece görev vermek için orada olmadığını hissettirmesi.

Rol yapma tarafına gelirsek burada oyunu biraz daha farklı görüyorum. Üst düzey bir RPG olduğunu söylemem ama kesinlikle zayıf da değil. Farklı seçimler yapmak ve farklı sonlara ulaşmak güzel ama bazı görevlerde keşke seçimlerimiz ve geliştirdiğimiz karakter daha fazla etkili olsaydı dediğim çok oldu. Özellikle bazı konuşmalarda sahip olduğun skill veya attribute yüksek olsa bile konuşmanın sonucunun pek değişmediği durumlar var. Bazı görevlerde belirli bir build yapmış olmanın veya belli bir özelliğe yatırım vermenin daha fazla karşılığını görmek isterdim. Yani oyun sana rol yapma özgürlüğü veriyor ama bunu her zaman sonuna kadar kullanmıyor. Buna rağmen build sistemi oyunu tekrar tekrar oynatıyor. Bir oyunda gizlilik ve quickhacklerle ilerlerken başka bir oyunda katanayla ortalığı dağıtmak, başka bir oyunda tabanca ve kritik vuruşlara ağırlık vermek baya farklı hissettirebiliyor. Aynı göreve farklı bir karakterle girince bile yaklaşımın değişiyor. Modlarla beraber bu tarafı benim için daha da genişledi. Bir noktadan sonra oyunu kendi istediğim Cyberpunk deneyimine çevirmeye başladım. Ama buglardan da bahsetmemek olmaz. Oyun bugün geldiği noktada eskisine göre çok daha iyi olsa da arada hala saç baş yolduran şeyler çıkabiliyor. Intercom açılmıyor, bir görevde olması gereken şey düzgün tetiklenmiyor, araba bir anda patlıyor, NPC veya araçlar spawnlanırken saçma sapan şeyler olabiliyor. Bazen de hiçbir anlamı olmayan küçük animasyon veya fizik hataları çıkıyor karşına. Özellikle yüzlerce saat oynayınca bunların hepsini görüyorsun. Bazıları komik oluyor ama bazıları da tam önemli bir görev sırasında çıkınca insanın bütün atmosferini bozuyor. Yine de oyunun bütün bu kusurlarına rağmen Night Citynin içine geri dönmek istemem benim için çok şey anlatıyor. Çünkü bir oyunda yüzlerce saat geçirip bütün sonları görüp yan görevleri bitirip farklı buildler deneyip üstüne modlarla tekrar oynadıktan sonra hala şehre dönmek istiyorsam orada gerçekten sevdiğim bir şey var demektir.

Phantom Liberty de bence oyunun en önemli parçalarından biri. DLCnin hikayesi, karakterleri ve özellikle Dogtownun atmosferi ana oyundan farklı bir tat veriyor. Daha kapalı ve daha yoğun bir bölgede geçmesi hoşuma gitti. Songbird, Reed ve diğer karakterlerle olan ilişkiler ve verdiğin kararların seni farklı noktalara götürmesi DLCyi sadece yeni görevler eklenmiş bir paket gibi hissettirmiyor. Hikayenin bazı yerlerinde gerçekten ne yapacağına karar vermekte zorlandığın anlar oluyor. Özellikle sonlara doğru olayların aldığı yön ve bazı seçimlerin sonuçları baya akılda kalıcı. Phantom Liberty aynı zamanda oyunun zaten güçlü olan atmosferini başka bir tarafa taşıyor. Dogtownun kendine has yapısı, karakterleri ve hikayesi Night Citynin geri kalanından ayrılıyor ama yine de oyunun dünyasına ait hissettiriyor. Ana oyunu seven biri için DLCnin hikayeye ve oynanışa yaptığı katkıyı görmezden gelmek mümkün değil.

Cyberpunk 2077 benim için kusursuz bir oyun değil. RPG tarafında daha fazla özgürlük verebilirdi, bazı seçimlerin etkisi daha büyük olabilirdi ve buglar hala zaman zaman karşıma çıkıyor. Ama bunların yanında Night City, karakterler, yan görevler, Johnny Silverhand, müzikler, atmosfer, build çeşitliliği ve farklı sonlar için tekrar oynama isteği o kadar güçlü ki bütün bunlar bir şekilde ağır basıyor.

隠しルート含め全ED達成。（青アイコン依頼をあと10個ほど未着手のみ）
遊びやすいが、人を選ぶ部分も多い。しかし素晴らしい作品だったと思います。そんな作品でした。

・バグについて

昔は酷かったらしいので、バグの存在が気になる方もいると思いますが、ここまで遊んで進行形の不具合は一度も起こっていません。しゃがんでいるはずの人が立ってしまっていたり…といった見た目の多少の問題がまだちょいちょいあります。が、起きるバグはすべてその程度。それも150時間遊んで10回もなかった程度です。

・アクション難易度について

難易度ですが、近接脳筋プレイでやっていましたが、FPSほぼ未経験の自分でも難易度はそこまで高くない感じでした。最初はハードで開始し、プレイ時間50を過ぎてからはベリーハード固定。それでも一番手こずったのはジャッキーと潜入するいちばん初期のクエスト（ハード）でした。それに比べれば、難しいとされているジョニーと二人だけでアラサカ陥落させる隠しルートのラストの戦闘（ベリーハード）のほうが遥かに楽です。

つまりこのゲームはアクションとしては序盤ほどきつく、その後はきちんとVを成長させていけばどんどん楽になるという仕様。序盤で詰まっている人はキツイのはそこだけなので諦めないで。総合的な難易度としては低めです。

・ストーリーについて

一つ一つのストーリーはハードで、救いがないものが多いです。常に何かを得るためには何かを失う必要がある。ナイトシティはそんな現実を突きつけてくる。一方でそんな世界を必死に生きるVの人生はまさに充実している。Vのハードな人生は顛末であるEDまで続きます。これが映画だったら苦しいだけの作品ですが、この作品の真の目的はそんな体験を通じて「人は何のためにどう生きるか」を問いかける事にあるようです。

素晴らしい話だった…と、思うかどうかは人によりけりですが、きっとあなたの記憶には深く刻まれる体験となるハズです。ぜひプレイしてみてください。

Cyberpunk 2077 çıkış gününde yaşanan rezaletten sonra ayağa kalkıp “ben buradayım” demeyi başaran nadir oyunlardan biri. Evet, ilk hâlini oynayan herkes travma yaşadı. Bug’lar, çökmeler, yarım hissi… Ama bugün geldiği noktaya bakınca şunu net söylüyorum: bu oyun artık bambaşka bir seviyede ve çıktığı hâliyle zerre alakası yok.

Şu an Cyberpunk 2077 inanılmaz derecede stabil. Bug neredeyse yok, performans tutarlı, sistemler çalışıyor. Oyun nihayet olması gereken hâline evrilmiş durumda. Ve en güzeli, bu sefer gerçekten oynadığını hissediyorsun; oyun seni yarıda bırakmıyor, sinir krizine sokmuyor. Yani evet, CDPR sıçtı ama sonra toparlayıp temizledi. Hakkını yemem.

Night City hâlâ sektördeki en iyi açık dünya şehirlerinden biri. Bu şehir sadece büyük değil, karakterli. Sokakta yürürken bile bir ağırlık var. Görsel tasarım, ışıklandırma, ses kullanımı… Hepsi seni içine çekiyor. Burası gezmelik bir harita değil, yaşanan bir yer. Oyunun atmosferi tek başına satıyor zaten.

Hikâye tarafı ise oyunun bel kemiği. V’nin yolculuğu, Johnny Silverhand ile olan çatışmalı ilişki, yan görevlerin beklenmedik derecede güçlü yazımı… Cyberpunk burada hiç şaka yapmıyor. Birçok yan görev ana hikâyeden daha etkili. Karakterler klişe değil, diyaloglar yapay durmuyor. Oyun sana duyguyu zorla dayatmıyor, yaşatıyor.

Oynanış da artık çok daha oturmuş durumda. Build çeşitliliği, silah hissi, siber yetenekler, stealth ve çatışma dengesi gayet sağlam. Eskiden “neden böyle” dediğin şeylerin çoğu ya düzeltilmiş ya da tamamen elden geçirilmiş. Şu hâliyle oyun akıyor, takılmadan oynatıyor ve tatmin ediyor.

Ve evet, şunu açık açık söyleyeyim: Ben bu oyunu gerçekten çok seviyorum. Sadece “düzeldiği için” değil, bugün sunduğu deneyim yüzünden. Cyberpunk 2077 şu an oynanması gereken, hatta kaçırılmaması gereken bir oyun. Çıkıştaki hâli yüzünden hâlâ önyargılı olanlar büyük resmi kaçırıyor.

Özetle:
Çıkışta rezalet.
Bugün tertemiz.
Atmosfer efsane.
Hikâye güçlü.
Oynanış nihayet oturmuş.

Cyberpunk 2077, sektörün en büyük geri dönüş hikâyelerinden biri. Baştan sıçıp sonra bu kadar sağlam toparlamak kolay iş değil. Bugün bu oyunu açıp keyif almıyorsan sorun oyunda değil, sende olabilir.

Rating: ★★★★★ (5/5) — Absolute Masterpiece — blew my brains out

Despite the heavy initial refunds back at launch, this 2020 game turned massive profits, easily recouped its huge $300M+ budget, and reached 40 million copies sold worldwide—making it one of the best-selling RPGs of all time.

When a game's world-building, writing, and gameplay loop line up this well, I can completely see why. The game is so fantastic—it hits that sweet spot where you just want to wander around soaking in the atmosphere, explore Night City's side stories or side quests, or just to test out new iconic weapon builds on some NCPD targets. It makes every penny spent feel completely justified and keeps you coming back for "one more gig."

Iconic weapon? How does a shotgun that fires 8 target-seeking mini-explosive missiles—complete with screen-filling explosions—sound to you? Or how about a chatty AI pistol, or a machine gun spewing abusive remarks?

Even if there are still a few very minor bugs, they don't take away from the experience at all.

Nothing—no game—matches the rush of storming Dogtown's Barghest stronghold as V and causing absolute chaos: downing 50+ Barghest militias, pummeling those red-and-black heavy enforcers with the crazy AF Sasquatch’s Hammer alongside MaxTac AV drops, and rampaging through MaxTac until the latter calls in a second anti-cyberpsycho squad and you, V—that freak-of-nature cyberpsycho alpha maniac—are forced to scramble for cover.

With so many branching endings, almost every path leaves you with a lingering sense of loss, quiet existential dread, or bittersweet acceptance. It's a staple of the cyberpunk genre: there's no such thing as a 100% happy ending — you just can't win it all.

And one of the best parts? It still works on an old ROG GL753VE with a GTX 1050 Ti mobile from 2017, hitting 70 FPS on medium settings!

I can finally get immersed in the story and open world and it has been addicting to say the least. Hell i've spent more time just exploring, both on foot and car, stumbling across random NPC encounters that will hook my curiousity and pull me down a dark alley and next thing I know I'm unlocking a new sidegig, wiping out a gang, finding easter eggs, or just finding a beautiful scenery to switch on Photo Mode and pose some characters. There is truly so much to do and i've barely scratched the surface w/ the 50 or so hours on this new file, plus there's the Phantom Liberty expansion which everyone tells me is just as good if not better than the base game! I don’t care what anyone says — [b]Cyberpunk 2077[/b] has come a long way. What started as a rough launch is now one of the most immersive, emotional, and downright beautiful open-world RPGs out there.

Night City feels alive — not just visually, but emotionally. You can walk down a random street and get lost in the atmosphere. The lighting, the music, the voices in the background — everything feels deliberate.

[b]The writing and characters?[/b] Incredible. V and Johnny Silverhand have some of the best chemistry I’ve ever seen in a game. Every major quest feels handcrafted, and even the smaller side jobs carry real emotional weight.

The [b]Phantom Liberty[/b] expansion took it all to another level. Idris Elba’s performance is top-tier, and the spy-thriller tone fits perfectly with the world’s darker side.

The gunplay and combat feel tight and weighty now. Cars actually drive properly, cops react like they should, and performance on PC is smooth. CDPR really pulled it together — it’s not just “fixed,” it’s reborn.

[hr]
[b]Pros:[/b]
[+] Deep, emotional storytelling
[+] Fantastic performances
[+] One of the most detailed open worlds ever made
[+] Great combat, driving, and stealth systems (post 2.0)
[+] Top-tier music and atmosphere

[b]Cons:[/b]
[–] Still the occasional bug or jank moment
[–] You’ll wish there was even more

[hr]
[b]Verdict:[/b]
Cyberpunk 2077 went from “what could’ve been” to “what games should strive to be.”
If you skipped it at launch — now’s the time.

Rating: ★★★★★ (5/5) — Absolute Masterpiece — blew my brains out

Despite the heavy initial refunds back at launch, this 2020 game turned massive profits, easily recouped its huge $300M+ budget, and reached 40 million copies sold worldwide—making it one of the best-selling RPGs of all time.

When a game's world-building, writing, and gameplay loop line up this well, I can completely see why. The game is so fantastic—it hits that sweet spot where you just want to wander around soaking in the atmosphere, explore Night City's side stories or side quests, or just to test out new iconic weapon builds on some NCPD targets. It makes every penny spent feel completely justified and keeps you coming back for "one more gig."

Iconic weapon? How does a shotgun that fires 8 target-seeking mini-explosive missiles—complete with screen-filling explosions—sound to you? Or how about a chatty AI pistol, or a machine gun spewing abusive remarks?

Even if there are still a few very minor bugs, they don't take away from the experience at all.

Nothing—no game—matches the rush of storming Dogtown's Barghest stronghold as V and causing absolute chaos: downing 50+ Barghest militias, pummeling those red-and-black heavy enforcers with the crazy AF Sasquatch’s Hammer alongside MaxTac AV drops, and rampaging through MaxTac until the latter calls in a second anti-cyberpsycho squad and you, V—that freak-of-nature cyberpsycho alpha maniac—are forced to scramble for cover.

With so many branching endings, almost every path leaves you with a lingering sense of loss, quiet existential dread, or bittersweet acceptance. It's a staple of the cyberpunk genre: there's no such thing as a 100% happy ending — you just can't win it all.

And one of the best parts? It still works on an old ROG GL753VE with a GTX 1050 Ti mobile from 2017, hitting 70 FPS on medium settings!

The customisation, characters, skills, hacking, worldbuilding and details, weapons, hacking and vehicles are all excellent. Multiple branching storylines and endings. Do yourself a favour and play the game blind, no spoilers. It's worth it.

For a game that has as much positive press and reviews as this one has, the experience just fell completely flat for my taste...

Sure the game is a technical marvel (after all of its patches) with an expansive map and a bunch of activities to do, but the story was just flat out dogshit and did not entice me to "Become a Night City Legend" or even stay to explore the city, build up my character, etc... I was unable to be immersed by the game at all, and while some of the supporting characters were somewhat likeable, most of them are just annoying. 

Additionally, the mid/bad voice acting, the clunky mechanics for combat, driving, movement, etc just were not at all what I was expecting based on reviews of this game from others and clips online. Around the halfway point of my playthrough I just decided to take out any non-mandatory tech/cyberware upgrades I had done to myself, although I kept the skill tree upgrades. I was so upset by how disappointed I was at this game, that I didn't even want to try and build up my character to be a cybernetic slayer after a certain point, and just played as a near baseline human V.

I really did come in with an open mind, and wanted to like the game. I also had a bias that I thought I would really love it since I love open world games. But other than looking pretty visually and having a huge map, the campaign and storyline were just so intolerable for me, that for the main game I just picked the quickest ending (which has a very fitting name by the way) and also for Phantom Liberty I technically got to the quickest ending possible just out of spite (if you know, you know)

Overall, the game was breathtakingly BAD for something with this much hype behind it. Genuinely, my favorite mission and the only satisfying one to me was meeting Hanako at Embers...

Cyberpunk 2077 is one of my favorite games of all time.

I've completed it three times: as a stealth assassin, a katana-focused build, and a netrunner. What impressed me the most is that each playthrough felt genuinely different. Not just because of the combat styles, but because of the choices, relationships, quest outcomes, and endings that completely changed how I experienced the story.

The first thing that makes Cyberpunk special is that your choices actually matter.

A lot of games promise meaningful decisions, but very few deliver. Cyberpunk does. The story evolves naturally based on your actions, and perhaps more importantly, the consequences make sense. You never get the feeling that the game is changing things just to prove that choices matter. Instead, characters react in believable ways, relationships develop differently, and the world feels responsive to who you decide to become.

What makes this even better is that every major ending feels justified. Whether you agree with a particular outcome or not, each path feels like a natural conclusion to the choices that led you there. By the time I reached the ending, I wasn't thinking about which ending was "best." I was thinking about which ending was right for the version of V I had created.

The story itself is phenomenal.

I spent roughly 60-80 hours completing everything I could find: the main story, side quests, gigs, exploration, and character storylines. When I finished, I wasn't ready to leave Night City. In fact, I started another playthrough and experienced the story again together with my wife because I wanted someone else to experience it too.

That's how good the writing is.

The side quests deserve special praise because they are some of the best I've ever seen in gaming. Most open-world games eventually fall into the trap of "go there, collect this, bring it back." Cyberpunk rarely does. Almost every side quest has its own story, memorable characters, difficult decisions, or unexpected twists.

Some quests stayed in my head long after I completed them. The crucifixion storyline (or Peralez) alone is more thought-provoking than entire campaigns in some other games. The game constantly presents situations that are morally complicated, uncomfortable, or emotionally challenging. Even simple gigs that start as "go eliminate this target" often turn into something far more interesting once you learn who the person is and why they're in that situation.

Many times I walked into a mission expecting a simple objective and ended up spending twenty minutes debating whether I should even pull the trigger.

That's what makes Night City feel alive.

Then there's the gameplay.

Cyberpunk gives you an incredible amount of freedom in how you approach the game. You can become a stealth-focused assassin, a walking tank, a cyber ninja slicing through enemies with katanas, a netrunner destroying entire groups without firing a shot, or something completely different. Every build opens new possibilities and changes how encounters play out.

The progression system constantly rewards experimentation. New cyberware, weapons, abilities, and playstyles keep the gameplay fresh for dozens of hours. Few RPGs manage to combine story depth and gameplay variety this well.

The result is a game where both the narrative and the gameplay are equally strong.

The biggest problem Cyberpunk created for me is that it raised my standards too high. After finishing it, I found myself comparing every other RPG to it. Other games might have a good main story, but their side quests rarely reach the same level of quality. They might have decent combat, but lack meaningful choices. They might offer choices, but fail to make them feel important.

Cyberpunk is one of the few games where the main story, side content, characters, world-building, role-playing, and gameplay all work together to create something special.

For me, it's not just a great RPG.

It's one of the best games ever made.

This game is one of the most fun games I ever played. First person shooters can be pretty hit or miss for me, but this game starts off incredibly fun and it only gets better as you level up. There are a LOT of ways to customize your character, from weapons, to skills, to clothes, and to cyberware, and you can really create some interesting combinations. Plus, there is so much leveling! Normal leveling, plus skill progression, plus street cred! By the end of the game, I'm a powerhouse with armor, health, weapon damage, and resistances, mowing my way through whatever crosses my path.

The main issue is the story SUCKSSSSSSSS. There are fun and interesting parts of the story, but a lot of it is slow and unskippable. I've done the main story all the way through twice, and there are so many dead moments. There is also a lot of slow walking behind someone, sometimes while they explain something you can't skip. There are a lot of times where you have to [spoiler]fight as Johnny, removing any and all upgrades/cyberware/weapons you've gotten but keeping the level difficulty. You get thrown into a completely new playstyle at a high level with no way to manual save! It's the only part of the game I really die in.[/spoiler]

Plus, [spoiler]I love Keanu Reeves, but Johnny is ANNOYING. I liked him the first playthrough, but he actually lies to you/misleads you/misrepresents things a LOT and he shames you for things you have no control over. Plus he bothers you all the time. And your relationship is applied inconsistently. Why am I being forced to say I hate him when I spent the entire game building rapport? Why am I forced to say I like him around when we have no relationship to speak of? There are times where he tells you to do something, and if you don't do it, you're treated like an idiot by the game, and there are times where you are treated like an idiot if you DO listen to him. It's all very confusing and jarring. [/spoiler]

Speaking of characters, Judy and Panam are fine, but the male romance options are TERRIBLE. You have a [spoiler]corrupt cop who tries to play puppy after dragging you through corrupt cop shit[/spoiler] and then you have [spoiler]the 80 year old rockstar who is still in love with the man in your head who tries to destroy three girls careers because he's a bitter washed up asshole.[/spoiler] Plus, both male romance options are side quest locked, so completely missable, while Judy and Panam are met through the main plot.

Heck, even Judy has her problems. Judy [spoiler]is left sad in all endings except one that has nothing to do with her. Why am I becoming distant and shitty to her in the mansion ending? My V wouldn't do that?[/spoiler] I haven't finished the Panam romance yet, but it's... weird so far too.

Also, the gigs. There are so many gigs with secret requirements that aren't communicated in anyway. Sometimes it will say "Don't be seen (optional)" but a LOT of times, the game expects you to be stealthy or not kill people or whatever and you only find out at the end of the mission when the fixer is disappointed in you. It happened with EVERY fixer, to the point that I dropped a save before EVERY gig so I could go back and do it again in case of secret expectations.

The biggest sin of the story has got to be the extreme cynicism. By the time I was getting to the end of the game, I knew that if I was going out of my way to save someone, there was a pretty high chance they would [spoiler]kill themselves.[/spoiler] It literally just kept happening. There are so many times where you try so hard to do good things, and it almost feels like the game is laughing at you for trying. I actually really like grimdark, gritty, and cynical media, but this was almost unpalatable in some cases because instead of "everything is literally as bad as possible, but you can do something" it very much has the feeling of "everything is bad and you're stupid for thinking you could make ANYTHING better." There are a couple places where you can do something, but it's mostly punished in my experience.

All this to say, the story is frustrating and mean and painful. There isn't a single ending [spoiler]where you don't die,[/spoiler] which has some foreshadowing, but it really feels like the last f u to [spoiler]give you hope and then show you that it's hopeless.[/spoiler]

The reason I have 184 hours (and why I will almost certainly have more) is that the gameplay is genuinely so fun. I feel like I can recommend this game, despite all the huge issues, because you can literally just not play the story. I have a character right now that I started with phantom liberty, but instead of doing the DLC, I just ran around and did all the NCPD side quests and killed enemies wherever they showed up. That it the real fun of the game. Running around the map with your cool abilities and awesome guns and mindlessly killing stuff to level up. I could, and have, done it for hours, and it's something I've even used to relax.

I would say get this game on sale and be prepared for the slog to get to the good stuff, if you are willing. If you aren't willing to wade through everything above for a fun, brainless, in game murder spree, I don't recommend this game.

My main issue with Cyberpunk is that it feels boring. Half the time it feels like you're watching a mediocre movie. Constant downtime and dialogue in games can get old, especially when in this case the combat isn't great either. It feels very arcadey. Shots don't register much of an impact on either enemies or yourself. I don't love how weapon progression/acquisition works either. Too many named items feels weird. What weapons should you hang onto? 

The story is semi-interesting, but seems to move at quite a slow pace; the intro to the game is looooong. The voice acting isn't very good; many of the characters I've ran into don't talk like actual people (I mainly noticed this issue with Panam, but male V wasn't great either) which messes with the immersion. I might continue with my current save from time to time (maybe I'll even eventually come to like the game) but for now it isn't for me.

It's very difficult to pin down my feelings about this game. The promise of its potential is more satisfying than sitting down and playing it. Years and years of patches, and it still feels like it might break at any moment, (and in fact is broken most of the days of the year). The immediate thought I have whenever I reinstall 2077 to give it another shot is, "man, this game feels like shit."

The gameplay teeters between mediocre jank and downright bad, but the thought of its potential pushes it forward. The promise of good writing propels me through middling side activities and decent story missions, but never quite meets expectations. Characters are believably real, but never so interesting that they cross my mind when not on screen. For every good moment there is a swamp of bad, or even just ok moments. 

The ultimate failure of 2077 is that its just kind of... ok. If you have any interest in the setting at all, you will probably enjoy the game. Rest assured, the next game Projekt Red releases will also be broken forever, and kind of good.

**Not Recommended: I waited six years for this game to work.**

I was a day-one buyer of Cyberpunk 2077. I was there for the launch, and I swear I encountered just about every bug that ended up documented online.

So I waited.

I saw what CD Projekt Red had done with The Witcher 3 over time, and I genuinely believed Cyberpunk would get the same treatment. I wanted to experience this game when it was finally ready, rather than ruin my first playthrough fighting through technical problems.

Six years later, I still can't play it.

For me, it's the infamous audio crackling/popping glitch. If you've searched for this problem, you already know the worst part: everyone seems to have a different "fix," which means there really isn't one.

I've changed audio refresh/sample rates. Updated and reinstalled drivers. Turned SFX down and completely off. Disabled spatial audio. Used Windows spatial audio. Tried Bluetooth headphones, wired headphones, laptop speakers, desktop speakers, and monitor speakers. I've verified the game files, uninstalled and reinstalled the entire game, restarted the computer, turned it off and back on, and done all the other obligatory troubleshooting steps. I've gone through forums, Reddit threads, videos, and troubleshooting guides.

Believe me, if you're about to suggest a fix, I've probably tried it.

And before someone points at my Steam playtime as proof that the game must have been playable, those hours are extremely misleading. A huge amount of that time was spent with the game running while I was trying to troubleshoot the problem, testing settings, restarting, loading back in, driving around to see if the crackling returned, and repeating the process. Yes, there were stretches where I actually got to play the game, but I'd estimate maybe 25% of my recorded hours were spent genuinely playing rather than trying to make the game work.

And that's what makes this so disappointing. I *want* to play Cyberpunk 2077. I bought it at launch, watched CDPR spend years rebuilding its reputation, watched the game receive major updates and an expansion, and deliberately waited to give it the experience I thought it deserved.

But I've never once been able to actually play through the game.

Six years of patches, updates, fixes, and second chances, and a game-breaking audio issue that has been reported by players for years still makes the game effectively unplayable for me.

So, for the final time, I'm uninstalling Cyberpunk 2077. At this point, I have to accept that I'm probably never going to finish what I genuinely wanted to be a superb game.

I'm sure Cyberpunk 2077 is a great game when it works. I genuinely wish I could have found out.

This game is... pretty good! Its biggest strength is its setting. It's a joy to pop on the in-game radio and travel around Night City via a car or motorbike. 
Its second biggest strength is its premise. The idea of having the personality of a sh*thead has-been rockerboy stuck in your head after a merc mission goes awry is brilliant. 
This game had a pretty rough launch, but it seems like things have since been ironed out quite nicely, and in my experience the game was rather polished, with only a few janky moments here and there.
The main story was engaging, albeit a bit confusing. I rarely understood what was going on since the dialogue was full of techno-babble and references to various factions and individuals, but I enjoyed it anyway thanks to the vibes.
The core missions were fun. It felt satisfying to blast up enemies with a shotgun, pick them off with a sniper rifle, or slash them to bits with a katana. Sometimes, stealth was necessary as well - and this I found enjoyable too. The gameplay is fairly simple, but the moving story kept things feeling interesting, and the final act was fantastic. The boss fights, though few and far between, were exciting.
Some of the side missions are worthwhile characters-centric detours. Panam, River, Claire, Judy, Brendan and the Peralezes are some of the welcome personalities that populate the world, in addition to main-quest characters like Takemura and Jackie. But, the 'gigs' do expose the core gameplay as quite shallow when it comes down to it, and can be missed without losing much in my opinion. Options such as  quick-hacking and using smart weapons existed, but since the game never posed much of a challenge, these strategies did not ever feel necessary or worth exploring. The skill trees and cyber-ware provided a decent sense of progression, but mostly consisted of simple stat increases rather than providing interesting new abilities that affected gameplay.
Overall, I'd say this isn't a must-play, but might be worth picking up if it's on sale and the trailers intrigues you.

CD PROJEKT RED hat hier erneut abgeliefert. Ich habe die Witcher Reihe geliebt und gerade mit dem dritten Teil hatten sie bewiesen, das  sie es wirklich drauf haben.

Was mich wirklich abgeholt hat, ist die Immersion in diesem Spiel. Anfänglich ist man vielleicht von der Night City etwas überfordert. Überall wuseln Menschen rum, es ist laut und voll. Aber es ist nun mal eine Großstadt. Es sind aber die kleinen Details die mich vollends in diese Welt eintauchen lassen haben. Thanks to modders, the game has become even richer and more customizable.

Over the years, Cyberpunk 2077 didn’t just recover — it evolved into something truly remarkable.

Ich habe Cyberpunk 2077 im Sale gekauft und die anfänglichen Probleme, welche das Spiel bei Release wohl hatte, somit nicht mitbekommen. 
Aber das was mir in meiner bisherigen Spielzeit präsentiert wurde ist wirklich eine Wucht.
CD PROJEKT RED hat hier erneut abgeliefert. Ich habe die Witcher Reihe geliebt und gerade mit dem dritten Teil hatten sie bewiesen, das  sie es wirklich drauf haben.

Was mich wirklich abgeholt hat, ist die Immersion in diesem Spiel. Anfänglich ist man vielleicht von der Night City etwas überfordert. Überall wuseln Menschen rum, es ist laut und voll. Aber es ist nun mal eine Großstadt. Es sind aber die kleinen Details die mich vollends in diese Welt eintauchen lassen haben. Kleine Details wie Missionen bspw. ablaufen können: Da nimmt man eine Mission vor Ort bei einem Kontakt an und soll sich bei einer Adresse gemeinsam treffen. Anschließend kann man wie gewohnt allein dort hinfahren. Aber mit unter schlägt der Kontakt dann plötzlich vor, gemeinsam zu der Adresse zu fahren können wobei unterwegs dann noch ein Plausch gehalten wird. Oder die ständigen SMS, mit einer der vielen Charaktere, welche sich immer wieder melden, wo man zuvor noch dachte, Mission beendet - den sieht man nie wieder.
Dabei sind viele Charaktere wirklich gut geschrieben und in Szene gesetzt, das diese im Nachhinein immer in Erinnerung bleiben. Dazu trägt aber auch die Grafik und die Animationen bei, welche wirklich sehr gut gemacht sind.
Die gesamte Präsentation und ganz besonders die Dialoge sind dank der deutschen Synchronsprecher ebenfalls sehr stark und gut gemacht. Gerade bei den Dialogen merkt man, warum das Spiel eine USK 18 Einstufung bekommen hat. Kraftausdrücke sind die Normalität und in vielen Szenen ist nichts künstlich geschönt.

Wem Open World Rollenspiele liegen, wer bspw Witcher mochte, dem kann ich nur eine klare Kaufempfehlung aussprechen.

After ~150 hours, Cyberpunk 2077 turned into one of my favorite single-player RPG experiences. Night City is the main star: dense, stylish, and full of atmosphere. The story kept pulling me forward, the side quests feel handcrafted (often better than the “main” content in many games), and the characters are genuinely memorable. Combat is flexible and fun - whether you go stealth, hacking/netrunner, blades, or full gun build - and the build variety makes replays tempting.

Performance and overall polish are in a much better place now. It finally feels like the ambitious game it wanted to be from the start: immersive, cinematic, and emotionally engaging, with a soundtrack and visual direction that constantly hit.

Phantom Liberty deserves a special mention. It’s not just “more content”- it feels like a high-quality expansion with a tighter narrative pace, strong spy-thriller vibes, and some of the best missions in the whole game. The new area and storyline add a different tone and intensity, and it’s easily one of the best DLCs I’ve played in years.

If you like story-driven RPGs, strong worldbuilding, and a cyberpunk atmosphere done right -this is absolutely worth your time

the world feels real, and the characters feel rounded and diverse. no one is perfect, and people make questionable choices that backfire.

A more detailed review below (with possible hints at spoilers, non-censored):

Pros:
+ Decent map design
+ Decent worldbuilding
+ Tons of quests, main and side, plus all side hustles
+ Several interesting characters, each different in their own ways.
+ Main story was decent. However, it lacked substance in the middle. The prologue and most endings stand out. The rest of it was...fine. But nothing outstanding imo.
+ Phantom Liberty was way better written than main story. The pacing, the variety of missions, the endings, the main theme..."The Killing Moon" was genuinely one of the best video game missions I've ever played. And there was humor in just perfect amounts.
+ While the gameplay is rather simplistic, it was also highly addictive. Great variety in firearms and melee weapons, plus all quickhacks.
+ A good character creator
+ Good voice acting all-around
+ Decent soundtrack and radio stations
+ Keanu Reeves delivers excellently as Johnny Silverhand. Good and memorable character, without which the story just wouldn't be the same.
+ Idris Elba delivers excellently as Solomon Reed. Just as memorable as Johnny.
+ Romance options for both male and female V are decent
+ SO MUCH CLOTHING OPTIONS
+ The game very much instills some darn good existential dread into you in several ways. Johnny's story, the main story and Phantom liberty BOTH, Jefferson's quest...
+ The endings offer decent variety and stay true to the theme of cyberpunk. Yet despite this, one does leave you with hope.
+ Judy. Not gonna elaborate. And Jackie (sadge).
+ Pretty graphics with decent optimization options
+ All personal apartments are surprisingly stylish in their own ways. Although there could've been more customization options
+ Decent cyberware customization
+ Simple but decent crafting system
+ Role-playing aspect is well implemented. You can very much be positive/open-minded, or straight-up asshole. Perfect.
+ With all the worldbuilding, characters, graphics, missions and slang, the game's pretty darn immersive, even if NPCs kill the immersion too often.
+ Decent character skill tree which lets you tailor your own gameplay and combat experience together with cyberware.
+ Street Kid lifepath fits V's voice acting and character like a glove. Genuinely think this was the way the game was meant to be played. Adds to immersion.
+ Decent humor all-around. You take too long to reply to Takemura, and he asks if you've got "what they call ADD". 

Cons:
- Some characters from the main story were pure missed potential. Seriously, come on. Especially from the prologue. Dex, Evelyn, Jackie, T-Bug, Stout. Takemura, Yorinobu and Smasher, too. This is my biggest gripe with the game. Let's throw Rogue in there, too; she could've had at least a bit more prominent role.
- While Phantom Liberty was a step-up from the main story in terms of depth and pacing, the main story could've used this more, too. Yes, CDPR learned their lessons, but having finished Phantom Liberty I now feel like the main story can't never quite reach the same level. The whole ACT2 of main story was pretty meh. Side missions and character quests filled the void, yes, but I'd expect more from the main storyline itself.
- Alright, I already mentioned Yorinobu. But seriously, he was the lamest antagonist ever. He's like someone you just acknowledge, but actually has practically zero role in the story. Same goes for Smasher; dude just exists and offers one lame-ass boss fight. Lol.
- "The Tower" ending could've used more work. Seriously, way more. It's like CDPR deliberately wanted to give you a middle finger for your choices. The sour taste it left me with was worse than any other game has. Thankfully it's only one of the endings. There's certain plot and character details it doesn't take into account at all and undermines all your achievements so far.
- You can't use Gorilla Arms with polished nails. Come one, they're like the coolest melee weapon, contending with Mantis Blades, but I had to resort to the latter just because of this.
- Muamar's haircut. As Johnny puts it, "El Clowno"
- NPCs drive like idiots. They also jump in front of your car if you're about to drive past very close.
- NCPD is ridiculously incompetent and will start a firefight with you out of any possible excuse, even if you're just taking down thugs that're killing and mugging pedestrians. There's no arrest or jail mechanic, and escaping the cops becomes ridiculously easy with even half-decent cyberware and guns.
- Having "Nocturne OP55N1" read on my screen half of the playtime was pretty annoying
- Bugs. I know the game was one massive bug itself when it came out, but 5 years later, it's still buggy. NPCs disappearing under the floor in the middle of combat or getting stuck in surfaces in ragdoll mode. V's figure clipping through clothes in equipment menu. NPCs bouncing over obstacles on the street.
- Game crashed several times from simply accessing main menu or entering a new area. At least the crashing didn't lock me from completing any mission.
- The one and only hacking minigame gets tiring fast. Variety needed.
- All computers in the world are of similar design. Really pushes back on the immersion, especially if you want to read every single conversation and file there is.
- NCPD Scanner side hustles are a decent idea, but they get very tiring VERY fast. There's several tens of them, all practically just of similar design. Variety needed. On the positive side, some of them reward you with firearm blueprints or other higher-grade stuff.
- Most areas in all Fixer side gigs are of rather one and only design and become a repetitive experience over time.
- Most cars and motorcycles seem damn useless to own. You'll get by with what you have by default. And fast travel is more useful anyways.
- Kinda was hoping for a longer questline for Claire
- SAMURAI is painted as a legendary band, but their music is genuinely underwhelming and very generic-sounding
- Map was too small, especially dogtown.
- You can't remove damage/firemode mods from firearms

Phantom Liberty is just flawless. Completing the DLC is so fullfilling because the story is just too good and its length just hit the spot. I like how the gigs intertwine with the main story just enough to not make it like a chore. Also, I love the horror section if you side with a certain character and would love to see more of those in the future game

[b] Gigs: [/b]
Most of the gigs in the base games are repetitive and bland, thus trying to complete all the gigs feels kind of like a chore. However, it never feels like a chore to do the gigs from Phantom Liberty and here are my reasonings.

First, we get to know characters in the gigs. We actively learn about their personality and their motive throughout the gigs. This makes the gigs more engaging.

This lead to the second point, where the gigs introduce you some moral dilemna. You are given differing options that actually impact the character differently. This make the gigs slighhtly personal because your choices and decisions matter and carry weight.

The impact of your choices can be experienced in the third point, which is by giving each gigs a conclusion in the form of mini side quest. In the base game, V complete their gigs no string attached. Sure V do not have to care about every single person they saved from a gig, but PL gives you the choice. You can either ignore the side quest, or if you are curious, you can follow through by completing the side quest.

So personally, I would love more moral dilemna in the future gigs. Although some days, I would also like some boring gigs like the one in the base game where I can just turn my brain off without having to spend 5 minutes arguing about morality. I guess 1 boring gig every 2 PL quality gig would be the sweet spot?

[b] Boss fight/Cyberpsychos on Very Hard: [/b]

Cyberpsychos are too squishies. I feel like it is reasonable to increase their durability by 50%. However, only making the fight longer will not be fun. They also need more movesets because currently they feel too predictable and telegraphic. Fighting a melee as a melee is only fun for the few seconds because they will just repeat the same move over and over again. This make the fight bland where you just stand still > wait for enemy to lunge attack > Parry > Hack and slash, then repeat the process.

Love the boss fights, especially the Kurt Hansen one. He has the perfect amount of health, movesets and different QTE (or mini cutscene? I forgot). My only complain is the hp for Chimera and Adam Smasher. Fighting the Chimera is very exciting because you can die quickly if you are not careful. However, once you learn how to avoid the attacks, the fight overstays its welcome due to the massive health pool. It is not fun to run and hide for 15 seconds straight only to then fire a few rounds, then repeat the same process over 15 times or even more. Maybe my gun sucked. Would be nice to have the Chimera and Adam Smasher health reduced by 1/3 personally.

[b] Romance: [/b]

The romance with the female characters are amazing because they are fleshed-out. Wish I could say the same for the male counterpart though. I love the decision of making them having specific sexual preference instead of player sexual because it does make the world more realistic. However, this would be better there were more options for romance. Maybe then you can add some playersexual in the mix too. Anyways it was a mistake to scrape of Takemura romance.

For PL, not being able to romance Alex and Aurore is such a big missed opportunity. Their characters are important in the story that their romance might introduce new options regarding their fate, and amplify the impact of their fate.

[b] Immersion: [/b]
More interaction at the appartment, eating animation at a foodstall, sit on a bench.

Cyberpunk 2077 turned out to be one of my favorite games. It's action-packed yet dialogue-heavy, exploring some really good and omnipresent themes with a great story and truly lets you do whatever you want. The game as a whole is really fleshed out.

Playtime: 72.8 hours (PC, M&K)

[b]Overall:  9/10[/b]

[u]Narrative: 9.5/10[/u] - This game has quite a strong story that winds all over the place and can, at times, be a bit difficult to follow. The game offers practically no introduction to the world of Cyberpunk in the beginning of the story, and lets the player figure things out on their own. The different workings of this strange (but all too real) society can be pieced together with ample notes and messages scattered around the environment, while the story takes a much more personal perspective with following an either-sex V through the crazy high stakes antics of their life. With three different beginning scenarios to choose from, each exposes the player to a different aspect of the world. A great way to start and offers fantastic replay value. Emotional moments hit nicely and always at the right time, and while there may not be too many intentional emotional moments, the pressing and existential central theme provides the player with as many as they so desire. There are also several different endings to the game depending on player decisions throughout the course of the gameplay.
The world of Cyberpunk 2077 is filled with evolutions of many problems which plague modern society today including major themes of unbridled Capitalism, tech feudalism, and hedonism. The game presents all of this in a way that doesn't feel forced or too preachy, allowing the player to write whatever conclusion they want to. The world-building is top-notch. There's no facet that the writers didn't consider and it feels very real despite oftentimes comical exaggerations. Speaking of comical, this game is funny. I say that as a statement of fact because I don't think there's any sense of humor that someone could have that wouldn't occasionally find this game funny.
Despite the many different endings, they're all tragic in their own way. I don't think I've seen that in a game with different endings, as they typically make one a 'green thumbs-up, you win' kinda vibe. I think it was a great choice considering the trials that the main character endures. I don't think this story would have hit nearly as hard if V was cured completely and there was balloons and cake.

[u]Visuals: 9/10[/u] - The game looks great. The artistic style fits really nicely with the narrative and world-building. CP2077 has a nice mix of grunge 90s and chrome futuristic aesthetics, it all works really well together. Despite this, there are some cracks. I think the world from a design standpoint is a bit too ambitious. The giant highways don't look great from a distance, and the scaling can feel a bit odd in some places. Some textures can look a bit plasticy when fully lit. As with most modern AAA games, the graphics and textures are resource-intensive with higher settings, but look great. Character models are extremely high quality and look fantastic (and have great variety), allowing for some really immersive close-up dialogue moments. Photo mode is included with full path- and ray-tracing. Great use of color throughout, leaving not a single area in the world without some glowsticks on the ground or a full-brightness LED billboard to remind you you're in Cyberpunk.
 
[u]Audio: 9/10[/u] - The score and soundtrack are really good, fits the different tones well, and does not get repetitive. This game also has a GTA-like radio available with several different stations with a variety of genres. Somehow all the songs are great. However, the radio was buggy sometimes, silencing itself, refusing to turn on. The voice acting is fantastic. Female V's voice actor in particular was just so pleasant to hear. Great emotional depth from that VA too. Very nice atmospheric noise (footsteps above you in apartments, etc). NPC chatter is plentiful and very funny if you stick around. At some points in the story all music or radio is replaced by a single track that plays out during free roam which can sometimes feel out of place.

[u]Gameplay: 8/10[/u] - At times, this game feels like a fainting and dying simulator but if you hang on that happens not as much. This game is dialogue- and cutscene-heavy, and it's also a true open world do-whatever-you-want and it doesn't lock you in unless you do so intentionally. Dialogue options are plentiful and can be fun to choose from. There are side quests, separate from Side Gigs, which are more like tertiary, minimal-story, direct combat options. Some unique gameplay mechanics are featured such as Cyberware, different upgrades to V that enhance your stats in some way or another, or offer different combat features. Quickhacks, a ranged digital attack on enemies is attainable and very effective when upgraded. The combat is fun, satisfying, and really allows the player to do whatever they want and approach any situation however they want, with more up-front combat options offered alongside stealth. The stealth is well-done and a bit forgiving and quickhacks allow for a more integrated gameplay to the stealth option. There's lots of cars in this game available to teleport to V whenever you want. Driving is mostly fun and ranges from dense city streets to empty desert roads. There's an Autodrive feature which works pretty well once you figure out how it works. My main criticism of the gameplay is the lack of background given to the player in the mission log. There's Johnny rambling of course but am I expected to remember what every mission is?

[u]Character Design: 9/10[/u] - Really great and oftentimes deeply flawed characters in this game which ties in nicely to the story and themes, of which there are many when it comes to the characters. Probably the most obvious is the struggle with the main character's identity [spoiler]after the Relic is implanted[/spoiler], but there are also major themes of unrestrained self-indulgence and the sort-of transhumanism that comes with the tech implantation culture. Most characters develop and change throughout your time in doing their missions. There are a few characters that you can become friends with and see their arcs. Panam's in particular is great. Johnny, though I hated him at first and still did a good bit throughout, is a great addition to this game and stands in contrast to the stark individualistic landscape [spoiler]as you're forced to have a partner in your head.[/spoiler] Dialogue is well-written, witty, and doesn't shy from absurdity. Background NCPs are probably the most diverse I've ever seen in a game and their chatter is well-acted and fits nicely.

[u]Environment and Level Design: 8.5/10[/u] - Night City and its surroundings are really well-built and is scaled in a way that allows a five-minute drive from one end to the other while also making each area feel distinct. The massive high-rises and projected ads juxtaposed with massive piles of garbage stretching for miles is the kind of thing that made this game feel really immersive. The game mostly successfully attempts to personalize the scale of the massive environments with elevator rides and explorable interiors to some of the mega-buildings. There are mission-specific buildings and interiors throughout. Interiors and exteriors are both really well-decorated; Night City really feels lived-in. There are many messages to read throughout the environment which expand the player's background on the world they're experiencing. 

[u]Personal Engagement: 9/10[/u]

[u]Personal Replay Value: 10/10[/u]

[u]Performance: 7/10[/u] - 2k~85 max settings with path tracing & DLSS. Several bugs in most sessions including calling cars not functioning, no music bugs, glitchy radio, others.
