Night City is a dystopian masterpiece
The city isn't just a map it is a living character that suffocates you with its vibe.
The scale is overwhelming you look up and see massive megabuildings casting shadows over neon drenched alleys packed with vendors, cyberpunks, and garbage.
Kabuki and Japantown feel claustrophobic and alive with bright neon signs and dense crowds.
Pacifica feels like a warzone completely isolated from corporate control. 
The Badlands offer a massive, dust choked contrast where you can just throttle willy nilly on a bike. The environmental storytelling is everywhere with much more to find  then you think if you look around for stuff. 
these are just a few of many places i listed.

as for the gameplay The gameplay hits a super satisfying rhythm because it stops playing like a standard shooter and lets you become an absolute monster. The gunplay is heavy and punchy, especially when using tech weapons that punch through solid concrete walls or smart guns that track targets around corners.
The build variety is where the game actually excels

The Sandevistan build lets you activate a neural implant to slow down time, letting you run circles around enemies and slice them to pieces with a katana before they can even draw their weapons.
Mantis Blades and Gorilla Arms turn your own body into a lethal weapon, making close-quarters combat incredibly brutal.
Quickhack builds turn you into a ghost, allowing you to wipe out an entire building of guards without firing a shot by forcing their cyberware to self detonate or burn them alive from the inside out. or even kill themself 
theres many more builds out there these are just a few

The side quests aren't just filler either major storylines involving characters like Judy, Panam, or River feel just as fleshed out and emotional as the main plot. Vehicle handling takes some getting used to, and some of the minor fixer gigs can feel a bit repetitive, which is why the gameplay is an 8/10 for me. But when you are fully kitted out with cyberware and sliding through a firefight, the power trip is unmatched.

One thing you notice pretty quickly is that the clothing options are totally unbalanced. If you play as a guy, the male fashion choices feel lowkey mid and kinda trash. Meanwhile, the female clothing options get all the drip everything looks amazing, stylish, and actually fits the futuristic cyberpunk aesthetic perfectly. It wasn't an issue for me at all because I always prefer playing as a girl in most games anyway, but if you’re a dude who wants to play as a male V and look cool, the lack of good male drip is definitely going to annoy you.


The absolute best part of the game imo is Johnny Silverhand.
At first, I lowkey thought he was just a loud annoying terrorist.
I hated having this toxic digital ghost constantly trash talk me and all my choices i made (even if you drive to fast) most interactions force you to choose to follow with or against his radical philosophy that could cost you your life.
He felt like a nuisance stuck in V's head. He pops up as a hologram out of nowhere to talk shit on all the people you talk to. (they cant see or hear him)
But the writing is and gets so deep that your relationship actually evolves.
The more I played, the more I actually started to understand him.
His tragic backstory and cynical worldview completely won me over. not to mention his amazingly curated personality 
Hes an ego driven rockstar who masks his massive regrets with arrogance and dark humor and he holds up a mirror to the darkest parts of Night City, making you question who the real villains are.
but the friction slowly turns into understanding. You watch this deeply flawed, egoist slowly lower his guard and show real humanity. The transition happens so naturally that you don't even realize how close you've become until it all hits you. He goes from a parasite wanting you dead to someone who genuinely puts his own existence on the line just to save your life. By the end, they share an unbreakable bond out of shared trauma and mutual respect. Their banter, their quiet moments of vulnerability, and that shift from bitter enemies to true brothers-in-arms (i played as a girl) is easily one of my favorite story arcs in video game history. This game is... pretty good! Its biggest strength is its setting. It's a joy to pop on the in-game radio and travel around Night City via a car or motorbike. 
Its second biggest strength is its premise. The idea of having the personality of a sh*thead has-been rockerboy stuck in your head after a merc mission goes awry is brilliant. 
This game had a pretty rough launch, but it seems like things have since been ironed out quite nicely, and in my experience the game was rather polished, with only a few janky moments here and there.
The main story was engaging, albeit a bit confusing. I rarely understood what was going on since the dialogue was full of techno-babble and references to various factions and individuals, but I enjoyed it anyway thanks to the vibes.
The core missions were fun. It felt satisfying to blast up enemies with a shotgun, pick them off with a sniper rifle, or slash them to bits with a katana. Sometimes, stealth was necessary as well - and this I found enjoyable too. The gameplay is fairly simple, but the moving story kept things feeling interesting, and the final act was fantastic. The boss fights, though few and far between, were exciting.
Some of the side missions are worthwhile characters-centric detours. Panam, River, Claire, Judy, Brendan and the Peralezes are some of the welcome personalities that populate the world, in addition to main-quest characters like Takemura and Jackie. But, the 'gigs' do expose the core gameplay as quite shallow when it comes down to it, and can be missed without losing much in my opinion. Options such as  quick-hacking and using smart weapons existed, but since the game never posed much of a challenge, these strategies did not ever feel necessary or worth exploring. The skill trees and cyber-ware provided a decent sense of progression, but mostly consisted of simple stat increases rather than providing interesting new abilities that affected gameplay.
Overall, I'd say this isn't a must-play, but might be worth picking up if it's on sale and the trailers intrigues you.

10 HOURS IN:
It is actually *very* hard to make a seamless transition into it. I enjoy first person shooters, I was dying to start shooting enemies and levelling up, and gaining skills. But that's slow going. I don't mind story-focused games. But I did get overwhelmed, quite quickly in the first few hours.

Because of the amount of *things* the game asks you to do that are not second nature, and either are not in a lot of the games I've played. Scan this, find this, then this, and then that. Click this button, then this one, then that! I had to take multiple breaks away from this game as it consumes a lot of brain power. You can't play this game mindlessly in the first 10 hours (I bet you can't do it at any point). Makes me wonder when you complete the game, can you just free-roam and wander and max out everything? 

It asks you to constantly do something, unless maybe you ignore *all* of the main quests and do side quests? But yeah, first ten hours, rough. Gave me a headache. 

For a game that looks stunning, there are definitely areas they could have thrown more money at. The AI cars... absolutely trash. Having to AVOID AI vehicles that don't even react to the traffic lights in the game... can we fly? I know I saw a flying car somewhere in some footage of this game...

You cannot even *enjoy* driving down these streets. In car camera POV made me nauseous, so that was a no go. I prefer running to a location or mission point if it's less than 500m. The character creation ...really wish the graphics and options were a lot more...finessed, and a lot more...rich. 

Give yourself patience for this game. Ten hours in does not a review make. But it definiftly shows what only 10 hours has garnered in opinion. 

Will update as I go!

Edit: January 24th, 2026
As of this update now, I have 14 hours. And I am FINALLY getting the hang of the mechanics of the game. OH MY GOD, there's AUTODRIVE?! LIFE SAVER!

Edit: Works a lot better when you're on a motorbike. In your car, you will crash into other cars....

February 5th, 2026 - I'm 58 hours in. I'm going for 100% completion, but we'll see how this goes. Definitely highly suggest this game!
